Then Abū Hurayrah said: Recite, if you wish: ﴿وإنِّي أُعِيذُها بِكَ وذُرِّيَّتَها مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ الرَّجِيمِ﴾. There are other wordings of this ḥadīth from Abū Hurayrah, this being one of them, and it has been narrated from other narrators.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: Zakariyyā took charge of her, and he entered upon her in the sanctuary and found with her grapes in a basket out of season. He said: "From where is this for you?" She said: "It is from God." He said: "Indeed He who provides you with grapes out of season is able to provide me with a child from the old, barren, sterile woman," ﴿هُنالِكَ دَعا زَكَرِيّا رَبَّهُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 38]. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr narrated from Qatādah who said: Maryam was the daughter of their chief and imam, and their rabbis disputed over her, so they drew lots with their arrows as to who would take charge of her; Zakariyyā was the husband of her sister, so he took charge of her, and she was with him and he nurtured her.

al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan narrated similarly from Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās and a group of the Companions. Ibn Jarīr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding "wa-kaffalahā Zakariyyā" that he said: he placed her with him in his sanctuary.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 3, verses 38–44 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, "hunalika" (*hunalika*, "at that place/time") is an adverbial expression used for both time and place. Its original use is for place. It has been said that it is used for time specifically, while *hunaka* (*hunaka*, "there") is for place. It has also been said that each of the two may be used in place of the other. The *lam* indicates distance, and the *kaf* indicates address.

The meaning is that he (Zakariyya) made his supplication in that place where he was standing, next to Maryam, or at that time, asking Allah to grant him good offspring. What prompted him to this was what he saw of Hannah's bearing of Maryam, although she had been barren. Thus he gained hope of a child, even though he was old and his wife was barren. Or what prompted him to this was what he saw of winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter with Maryam, because whoever brings that about out of its season is able to bring about a child from a barren woman. On this view, this statement is a new narrative inserted within the story of Maryam because of the connection between them. *Dhurriyyah* (*dhurriyyah*, "offspring") and *nasl* (*nasl*, "progeny") may be used for the singular and for the plural, and the text indicates that it is singular here. His saying, ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir﴾, uses "waliyyan" (*waliyyan*, "an heir") and not "awliya'" (*awliya'*, "heirs"). The feminine form of "tayyibah" (*tayyibah*, "good") is because the word "dhurriyyah" is feminine.

His saying, ﴿Then the angels called him﴾: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "fa-nadahu" (*fa-nadahu*, "then he called him"), and Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud also read it this way. The rest read ﴿fa-nadathu al-malaikah﴾ (*fa-nadathu al-malaikah*, "then the angels called him"). It has been said that the intended one here is Jibril (Gabriel), and that using a plural form for a singular is permissible in Arabic. Among its examples is ﴿those to whom the people said﴾ [Al 'Imran: 173]. It has also been said that all of the angels called him, and this is the apparent meaning from attributing the verb to a plural. The literal meaning takes precedence, so one does not turn to a metaphorical meaning except with an indicator.

His saying, "wa-huwa qa'im" (*wa-huwa qa'im*, "while he was standing"), is a circumstantial clause (*jumlah haliyyah*). ﴿Praying in the niche﴾ is either a description of "qa'im" or a second predicate of "wa-huwa."

His saying, ﴿that Allah gives you good news﴾: it is read with the *fath* on *anna* (*anna*, "that"), with the implied meaning "bi-anna Allah" (*bi-anna Allah*, "that Allah"). It is also read with the *kasrah* on it, as if there were an implied verb of saying. The people of Medina read "yubashshiruka" (*yubashshiruka*, "gives you good news") with the doubled letter (shaddah). Hamzah read it with the lightened form. Humayd ibn Qays al-Makki read it with the *kasrah* and the *dammah* on the present-tense prefix letter.

Al-Akhfash said: these are three dialects with one meaning. The first reading is the one that occurs frequently in the Qur'an, such as ﴿So give good news to My servants﴾ [al-Zumar: 17], ﴿So give him good news of forgiveness﴾ [Ya-Sin: 11], ﴿So We gave her good news of Ishaq﴾ [Hud: 71], and ﴿They said: We give you good news of the truth﴾ [al-Hijr: 55]. This is the reading of the majority. The second is the dialect of the people of Tihamah, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud also read in this way. The third is from *abshara yubshiru ibsharan* (*abshara yubshiru ibshaaran*).

"Yahya" (*Yahya*) cannot take nunation, either because it is non-Arabic or because it has the form of a verb, like "ya'mar," together with being a proper name.

Al-Qurtubi, quoting from al-Naqqash, said: his name in the earlier Book was "Hanna," and that is the end of the quotation. What we have seen in several places in the Gospel is that his name is "Yuhanna" (John). It has been said that he was so named because Allah gave him life through faith and prophethood. It has also been said that he was so named because Allah gave life to people through him with guidance. The meaning here is the announcement of his birth, that is, "He gives you good news of the birth of Yahya."

His saying, ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾, means with 'Isa (peace be upon him). He was called "the word of Allah" because he came into being by the saying of the Exalted: "Be!" It has also been said that he was called "the word of Allah" because people are guided by him just as they are guided by the speech of Allah.

Abu 'Ubayd said: the meaning of ﴿a word from Allah﴾ is "a book from Allah." He said: the Arabs say, "He recited to me his *kalimah*," meaning his poem, just as it is narrated that al-Huwaydirah was mentioned to Hassan, and he said: "May Allah curse his *kalimah*," meaning his poem. That is the end of the quotation.

Yahya was the first to believe in and confirm 'Isa, and he was older than 'Isa by three years. It has also been said by six months. "Sayyid" (*sayyid*, "a leader") is one who leads his people. Al-Zajjaj said: the *sayyid* is one who surpasses his peers in every kind of goodness. "Haswur" (*haswur*, "one who restrains himself") is originally from *hasr*, which means confinement. It is said: "*hasarani al-shay'*" and "*ahsarani*" when a thing confines me. From this is the saying of the poet:

Nor is the separation from Layla that she has drifted away from you,
Nor that preoccupations have confined you.

A "hasur" is one who does not approach women, as if he withholds himself from them. It is said: "a man is *hasur* and *hasir*" when he withholds his gift and does not give it out. So Yahya (peace be upon him) was *hasur* from approaching women, that is, he was restrained and did not approach them as other men do, either because he lacked the ability to do so, or because he restrained himself from them, avoiding desire while having the ability. The second has been preferred, since the context is one of praise, and praise is only for something acquired, which its doer could have done otherwise, not for what is part of one's natural creation and innate disposition.

His saying, ﴿of the righteous﴾: that is, arising from the righteous, because he was from the lineage of the prophets, or being one of the righteous, as in His saying, ﴿and indeed in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah: 130]. Al-Zajjaj said: the righteous one is the one who fulfills to Allah what He has made obligatory upon him, and to people their rights.

His saying, ﴿He said: My Lord, how will I have a boy?﴾: The apparent meaning of this is that the address was from him to Allah, the Exalted, even though the message reaching him came through the angels. This is due to his great humility and eagerness in seeking an answer to his request. It has been said that by "Lord" he meant Jibril, that is, "O my master." It has been said that there are two possible meanings of this question. One is that he asked whether this child would be given to him from his barren wife or from someone else. It has also been said that the meaning is: by what cause do I deserve this, while I and my wife are in this condition? The summary is that he considered the child's coming into being from the two of them unlikely, since custom dictates that such a couple does not produce offspring. This was because on the day of the good news he was old. It has been said he was ninety years old, and it has been said he was a hundred and twenty years old, and his wife was ninety-eight years old. For this reason he said, ﴿And old age has overtaken me﴾, meaning, while this is the case. He made old age like one seeking him, because it is a forerunner of the vanguard of death, so he attributed the verb to it. "Al-'aqir" (*al-'aqir*, "barren") is the one who does not bear children, that is, one who has barrenness by nature. If it had been in the form of a verb, he would have said "'aqirah" (a barren woman in the feminine verbal form), meaning that she has a barrenness that prevents her from having children. This question was asked by him after his supplication that Allah grant him good offspring, and after witnessing that great sign regarding Maryam, as a way of magnifying the power of Allah, the Exalted, and not out of mere disbelief. It has also been said that after his supplication he had waited, until the time that his Lord willed, forty years, and it has been said twenty years. So the astonishment was from this perspective.

His saying, ﴿Thus does Allah do what He wills﴾: that is, Allah does what He wills of wondrous acts like that act, which is bringing forth a child from an old man and a barren woman. The *kaf* (*kaf*, "like") is in the position of an accusative as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, and the demonstrative refers to the verbal noun of "yaf'alu" (*yaf'alu*, "does"). Or the *kaf* is in the position of a nominative as a predicate, meaning: in this wondrous affair, the affair of Allah, and His saying "yaf'alu ma yasha'" (*yaf'alu ma yasha'*, "does what He wills") is an explanation of it. Or the *kaf* is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, meaning: Allah does the act being like that.

His saying, ﴿He said: My Lord, make for me a sign﴾, that is, a sign by which I know the validity of the pregnancy, so that I may receive this blessing with gratitude. ﴿He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture﴾: that is, your sign is that you restrain your tongue from speaking to people for three days, but not from other kinds of remembrance. The reason for making this the sign is so that those days would be devoted to the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, in gratitude for what He bestowed upon him. It has been said that this was a punishment from Allah, the Exalted, upon him, because of his request for a sign after the angels had spoken to him directly. Al-Qurtubi related this from most of the commentators.

"Al-ramz" (*al-ramz*, "gesture") in the language means signaling with the two lips, or the two eyes, or the two eyebrows, or the two hands. Its origin is movement. This is an exception of disjunction (*istithna' munqati'*), because the gesture is not of the same kind as speech. It has been said that it is a connected exception (*istithna' muttasil*), in the sense that speech is whatever conveys understanding, whether by word, sign, or writing. But this is far-fetched. The correct view is the first, and this is what al-Akhfash and al-Kisa'i said.

His saying, ﴿and glorify [your Lord]﴾: that is, glorify Him in the evening, "al-'ashiyy" (*al-'ashiyy*, "evening"), which is the plural of "'ashiyyah." It has been said that it is singular, and it is from the time the sun declines until it sets. It has been said it is from 'Asr until the passing of the first part of the night, and this is very weak. "Al-ibkar" (*al-ibkar*, "morning") is from the rising of dawn until the time of forenoon. It has been said that the intended meaning of glorification is prayer.

His saying, ﴿When the angels said: O Maryam﴾: the adverbial clause is connected to an omitted element, like the first adverbial clause. ﴿Indeed Allah has chosen you﴾: He selected you and purified you from disbelief, or from defilement, in its general sense. ﴿And chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾. It has been said that this second choosing is other than the first choosing. The first is when He accepted her with a good acceptance, and the second is for the birth of 'Isa. The intended meaning of "the worlds" here has been said to be the women of her own age, which is the correct view. It has been said it means the women of all the worlds until the Day of Resurrection, and al-Zajjaj chose this view. It has also been said that the second choosing is an emphasis of the first, and both refer to one thing.

His saying, ﴿O Maryam, be devoted to your Lord﴾: that is, prolong standing in prayer, or be constant. The meanings of *qunut* (*qunut*, "devotion") have already been discussed. He placed prostration before bowing because it is more excellent, or because their prayer had no fixed order, and the *wa* (*wa*, "and") is merely for joining without ordering.

His saying, ﴿and bow with those who bow﴾: its apparent meaning is that her bowing is together with their bowing, which indicates the legislation of congregational prayer. It has also been said that the meaning is that she does the same as their action, even if she did not pray with them. The reference in His saying "dhalika" (*dhalika*, "that") is to what preceded of the matters Allah informed about. Revelation (*wahy*, "revelation") in the language is informing in concealment. It is said: "wahy" and "awha" with the same meaning. Ibn Faris said: revelation is gesture, writing, message, and whatever you cast to another until you inform him.

His saying, ﴿And you were not with them﴾: that is, you were not present with them, meaning those who disputed over the upbringing of Maryam. He negated his presence with them even though it was known, because they denied the revelation. If that denial had been valid, there would have remained no way to know it except by witnessing and presence, and they do not claim that. Thus it is established that it was revelation, along with their acknowledgment that he was not one who reads the Torah nor one who associates with its people. "Al-aqlam" (*al-aqlam*, "the pens") is the plural of "qalam" (*qalam*, "pen"), from *qalamahu* when he cut it, meaning: pens with which they write. It has also been said they are arrows used for drawing lots. ﴿Which of them would take charge of Maryam﴾: that is, nurse her, meaning: they cast their pens to know which of them would take charge of her. This occurred during their dispute over her guardianship. Zakariyya said: he has the most right to her, since her maternal aunt was with him, and she was Ash'a, the sister of Hannah, the mother of Maryam. The children of Israel said: we have the most right to her, since she is the daughter of our scholar. So they drew lots and placed their pens in the flowing water, on the basis that whoever's pen stood still and did not flow with the water would be her guardian. Their pens flowed, and Zakariyya's pen stood still. Those who affirm the drawing of lots have used this as evidence, and the disagreement regarding that is well known. Authentic hadiths have been established regarding its validity.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: when Zakariyya saw that, meaning summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer with Maryam, he said: "Indeed the One who brought this to Maryam out of its season is able to grant me a child." That was when he called upon his Lord. Ibn 'Asakir related similarly from al-Hasan. Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi regarding ﴿good offspring﴾, that he said: "blessed."

Ibn Jarir related from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad, who said: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "Then Jibril called him while he was standing and praying in the niche." Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi that he said: ﴿Then the angels called him﴾ means Jibril. Ibn al-Mundhir related from al-Suddi, who said: "al-mihrab" (*al-mihrab*, "the niche") is the place of prayer. Al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn 'Umar that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of these altars," meaning the sanctuaries (*al-mahareeb*). Ibn Abi Shaybah related in al-Musannaf from Musa al-Juhani, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My community will remain in goodness as long as they do not take altars in their mosques like the altars of the Christians."

It has been related that the disapproval of this (naming him Yahya) was reported from a group of the Companions. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah that he said: "He was named Yaḥyā only because Allah gave him life (aḥyāhu) through faith."

They also related from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾, that he said: "ʿĪsā ibn Maryam is the Word."

Ibn Jarīr related through the route of Ibn Jurayj from him, who said: "Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā were cousins on the mother's side. Yaḥyā's mother used to say to Maryam: 'I find that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb.' That is his confirmation of ʿĪsā, his prostration in his mother's womb, and he was the first to confirm ʿĪsā."

Aḥmad, in the *Kitāb al-Zuhd* (the Book of Asceticism), and Ibn Jarīr related a similar report from Mujāhid. Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿and a master﴾ that he said: "forbearing and pious." ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid that he said: "al-sayyid is the one noble before Allah." Ibn Jarīr related from Ibn al-Musayyab that he said: "al-sayyid is the jurist, the learned."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying ﴿and a master and chaste﴾, that he said: "al-sayyid is the forbearing, and al-ḥaṣūr is the one who does not approach women." Aḥmad in the *Zuhd* related the same from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning al-ḥaṣūr. Aḥmad in the *Zuhd*, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "al-ḥaṣūr is the one who does not emit semen (lā yunzilu al-māʾ)." Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "His member was like the fringe of a garment (hudbat al-thawb)."

Ibn Abī Shaybah and Aḥmad in the *Zuhd* related it by another route from Ibn ʿAmr as a statement of his own (mawqūfan), and this is stronger.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Shuʿayb al-Jubbāʾī that he said: "The name of Yaḥyā's mother was Ashyaʿ." Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj concerning His saying ﴿Make for me a sign﴾ that he said: "By the conception of him (al-ḥaml bihi)."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah concerning His saying ﴿He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days"﴾ that he said: "He was punished with this only because the angels addressed him directly (shāfahat) with this, giving him good news of Yaḥyā. So he asked for the sign after the angels' speech to him, and so his tongue was restrained."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying ﴿except by gesture (ramzan)﴾ that he said: "The ramz is with the two lips." ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related the same from Mujāhid. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he said: "The ramz is signalling (al-ishārah)."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning (bi-l-ʿashiyyi wa-l-ibkār)﴾ that he said: "al-ʿashiyy is the sun's inclining until it sets, and al-ibkār is the beginning of dawn."

It is established in the two *Ṣaḥīḥs* (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and others, from the hadith of ʿAlī, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The best of its women is Maryam bint ʿImrān, and the best of its women is Khadījah bint Khuwaylid.'" al-Ḥākim related and authenticated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The best of the women of the worlds are Khadījah, Fāṭimah, Maryam and Āsiyah the wife of Pharaoh.'" Ibn Mardawayh related a similar report from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī (who authenticated it), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Ḥibbān and al-Ḥākim related a similar report from the hadith of Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). In the two *Ṣaḥīḥs* and others, from the hadith of Abū Mūsā, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Many men have become perfect, but among women none has become perfect except Maryam bint ʿImrān and Āsiyah the wife of Pharaoh. And the excellence of ʿĀʾishah over women is like the excellence of tharīd over (other) food.'"

There are many hadiths with this meaning, and all of them indicate that Maryam (peace be upon her) is the mistress of the women of her own world, not of the women of all the worlds. This is supported by what Ibn ʿAsākir related from Muqātil, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Four women are the mistresses of the women of their worlds: Maryam bint ʿImrān, Āsiyah bint Muzāḥim, Khadījah bint Khuwaylid, and Fāṭimah bint Muḥammad, and the most excellent of them in knowledge is Fāṭimah."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾ that he said: "Prolong the rukūd, meaning the standing (al-qiyām)." Ibn Jarīr related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning ﴿be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾ that he said: "Be sincere." He also related from Qatādah that he said: "Obey your Lord."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related through the route of al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens﴾ that he said: "When Maryam was placed in the mosque, the people of the place of prayer (ahl al-muṣallā), who were writing down the revelation, drew lots over her, casting their pens to determine which of them would take charge of her. Allah said to Muḥammad ﴿And you were not with them﴾, and so on." Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿIkrimah that he said: "They cast their pens into the water, and they went with the current, and the pen of Zakariyyā rose up, so Zakariyyā took charge of her." Ibn Jarīr related a similar report from al-Rabīʿ.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd related from Mujāhid, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim likewise related from Ibn Jurayj, that the pens were those with which they wrote the Torah. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿAṭāʾ that they were the arrows (al-qidāḥ, used for divination).

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 3, verses 38–44 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, "hunalika" (*hunalika*, "at that place/time") is an adverbial expression used for both time and place. Its original use is for place. It has been said that it is used for time specifically, while *hunaka* (*hunaka*, "there") is for place. It has also been said that each of the two may be used in place of the other. The *lam* indicates distance, and the *kaf* indicates address.

The meaning is that he (Zakariyya) made his supplication in that place where he was standing, next to Maryam, or at that time, asking Allah to grant him good offspring. What prompted him to this was what he saw of Hannah's bearing of Maryam, although she had been barren. Thus he gained hope of a child, even though he was old and his wife was barren. Or what prompted him to this was what he saw of winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter with Maryam, because whoever brings that about out of its season is able to bring about a child from a barren woman. On this view, this statement is a new narrative inserted within the story of Maryam because of the connection between them. *Dhurriyyah* (*dhurriyyah*, "offspring") and *nasl* (*nasl*, "progeny") may be used for the singular and for the plural, and the text indicates that it is singular here. His saying, ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir﴾, uses "waliyyan" (*waliyyan*, "an heir") and not "awliya'" (*awliya'*, "heirs"). The feminine form of "tayyibah" (*tayyibah*, "good") is because the word "dhurriyyah" is feminine.

His saying, ﴿Then the angels called him﴾: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "fa-nadahu" (*fa-nadahu*, "then he called him"), and Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud also read it this way. The rest read ﴿fa-nadathu al-malaikah﴾ (*fa-nadathu al-malaikah*, "then the angels called him"). It has been said that the intended one here is Jibril (Gabriel), and that using a plural form for a singular is permissible in Arabic. Among its examples is ﴿those to whom the people said﴾ [Al 'Imran: 173]. It has also been said that all of the angels called him, and this is the apparent meaning from attributing the verb to a plural. The literal meaning takes precedence, so one does not turn to a metaphorical meaning except with an indicator.

His saying, "wa-huwa qa'im" (*wa-huwa qa'im*, "while he was standing"), is a circumstantial clause (*jumlah haliyyah*). ﴿Praying in the niche﴾ is either a description of "qa'im" or a second predicate of "wa-huwa."

His saying, ﴿that Allah gives you good news﴾: it is read with the *fath* on *anna* (*anna*, "that"), with the implied meaning "bi-anna Allah" (*bi-anna Allah*, "that Allah"). It is also read with the *kasrah* on it, as if there were an implied verb of saying. The people of Medina read "yubashshiruka" (*yubashshiruka*, "gives you good news") with the doubled letter (shaddah). Hamzah read it with the lightened form. Humayd ibn Qays al-Makki read it with the *kasrah* and the *dammah* on the present-tense prefix letter.

Al-Akhfash said: these are three dialects with one meaning. The first reading is the one that occurs frequently in the Qur'an, such as ﴿So give good news to My servants﴾ [al-Zumar: 17], ﴿So give him good news of forgiveness﴾ [Ya-Sin: 11], ﴿So We gave her good news of Ishaq﴾ [Hud: 71], and ﴿They said: We give you good news of the truth﴾ [al-Hijr: 55]. This is the reading of the majority. The second is the dialect of the people of Tihamah, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud also read in this way. The third is from *abshara yubshiru ibsharan* (*abshara yubshiru ibshaaran*).

"Yahya" (*Yahya*) cannot take nunation, either because it is non-Arabic or because it has the form of a verb, like "ya'mar," together with being a proper name.

Al-Qurtubi, quoting from al-Naqqash, said: his name in the earlier Book was "Hanna," and that is the end of the quotation. What we have seen in several places in the Gospel is that his name is "Yuhanna" (John). It has been said that he was so named because Allah gave him life through faith and prophethood. It has also been said that he was so named because Allah gave life to people through him with guidance. The meaning here is the announcement of his birth, that is, "He gives you good news of the birth of Yahya."

His saying, ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾, means with 'Isa (peace be upon him). He was called "the word of Allah" because he came into being by the saying of the Exalted: "Be!" It has also been said that he was called "the word of Allah" because people are guided by him just as they are guided by the speech of Allah.

Abu 'Ubayd said: the meaning of ﴿a word from Allah﴾ is "a book from Allah." He said: the Arabs say, "He recited to me his *kalimah*," meaning his poem, just as it is narrated that al-Huwaydirah was mentioned to Hassan, and he said: "May Allah curse his *kalimah*," meaning his poem. That is the end of the quotation.

Yahya was the first to believe in and confirm 'Isa, and he was older than 'Isa by three years. It has also been said by six months. "Sayyid" (*sayyid*, "a leader") is one who leads his people. Al-Zajjaj said: the *sayyid* is one who surpasses his peers in every kind of goodness. "Haswur" (*haswur*, "one who restrains himself") is originally from *hasr*, which means confinement. It is said: "*hasarani al-shay'*" and "*ahsarani*" when a thing confines me. From this is the saying of the poet:

Nor is the separation from Layla that she has drifted away from you,
Nor that preoccupations have confined you.

A "hasur" is one who does not approach women, as if he withholds himself from them. It is said: "a man is *hasur* and *hasir*" when he withholds his gift and does not give it out. So Yahya (peace be upon him) was *hasur* from approaching women, that is, he was restrained and did not approach them as other men do, either because he lacked the ability to do so, or because he restrained himself from them, avoiding desire while having the ability. The second has been preferred, since the context is one of praise, and praise is only for something acquired, which its doer could have done otherwise, not for what is part of one's natural creation and innate disposition.

His saying, ﴿of the righteous﴾: that is, arising from the righteous, because he was from the lineage of the prophets, or being one of the righteous, as in His saying, ﴿and indeed in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah: 130]. Al-Zajjaj said: the righteous one is the one who fulfills to Allah what He has made obligatory upon him, and to people their rights.

His saying, ﴿He said: My Lord, how will I have a boy?﴾: The apparent meaning of this is that the address was from him to Allah, the Exalted, even though the message reaching him came through the angels. This is due to his great humility and eagerness in seeking an answer to his request. It has been said that by "Lord" he meant Jibril, that is, "O my master." It has been said that there are two possible meanings of this question. One is that he asked whether this child would be given to him from his barren wife or from someone else. It has also been said that the meaning is: by what cause do I deserve this, while I and my wife are in this condition? The summary is that he considered the child's coming into being from the two of them unlikely, since custom dictates that such a couple does not produce offspring. This was because on the day of the good news he was old. It has been said he was ninety years old, and it has been said he was a hundred and twenty years old, and his wife was ninety-eight years old. For this reason he said, ﴿And old age has overtaken me﴾, meaning, while this is the case. He made old age like one seeking him, because it is a forerunner of the vanguard of death, so he attributed the verb to it. "Al-'aqir" (*al-'aqir*, "barren") is the one who does not bear children, that is, one who has barrenness by nature. If it had been in the form of a verb, he would have said "'aqirah" (a barren woman in the feminine verbal form), meaning that she has a barrenness that prevents her from having children. This question was asked by him after his supplication that Allah grant him good offspring, and after witnessing that great sign regarding Maryam, as a way of magnifying the power of Allah, the Exalted, and not out of mere disbelief. It has also been said that after his supplication he had waited, until the time that his Lord willed, forty years, and it has been said twenty years. So the astonishment was from this perspective.

His saying, ﴿Thus does Allah do what He wills﴾: that is, Allah does what He wills of wondrous acts like that act, which is bringing forth a child from an old man and a barren woman. The *kaf* (*kaf*, "like") is in the position of an accusative as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, and the demonstrative refers to the verbal noun of "yaf'alu" (*yaf'alu*, "does"). Or the *kaf* is in the position of a nominative as a predicate, meaning: in this wondrous affair, the affair of Allah, and His saying "yaf'alu ma yasha'" (*yaf'alu ma yasha'*, "does what He wills") is an explanation of it. Or the *kaf* is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, meaning: Allah does the act being like that.

His saying, ﴿He said: My Lord, make for me a sign﴾, that is, a sign by which I know the validity of the pregnancy, so that I may receive this blessing with gratitude. ﴿He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture﴾: that is, your sign is that you restrain your tongue from speaking to people for three days, but not from other kinds of remembrance. The reason for making this the sign is so that those days would be devoted to the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, in gratitude for what He bestowed upon him. It has been said that this was a punishment from Allah, the Exalted, upon him, because of his request for a sign after the angels had spoken to him directly. Al-Qurtubi related this from most of the commentators.

"Al-ramz" (*al-ramz*, "gesture") in the language means signaling with the two lips, or the two eyes, or the two eyebrows, or the two hands. Its origin is movement. This is an exception of disjunction (*istithna' munqati'*), because the gesture is not of the same kind as speech. It has been said that it is a connected exception (*istithna' muttasil*), in the sense that speech is whatever conveys understanding, whether by word, sign, or writing. But this is far-fetched. The correct view is the first, and this is what al-Akhfash and al-Kisa'i said.

His saying, ﴿and glorify [your Lord]﴾: that is, glorify Him in the evening, "al-'ashiyy" (*al-'ashiyy*, "evening"), which is the plural of "'ashiyyah." It has been said that it is singular, and it is from the time the sun declines until it sets. It has been said it is from 'Asr until the passing of the first part of the night, and this is very weak. "Al-ibkar" (*al-ibkar*, "morning") is from the rising of dawn until the time of forenoon. It has been said that the intended meaning of glorification is prayer.

His saying, ﴿When the angels said: O Maryam﴾: the adverbial clause is connected to an omitted element, like the first adverbial clause. ﴿Indeed Allah has chosen you﴾: He selected you and purified you from disbelief, or from defilement, in its general sense. ﴿And chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾. It has been said that this second choosing is other than the first choosing. The first is when He accepted her with a good acceptance, and the second is for the birth of 'Isa. The intended meaning of "the worlds" here has been said to be the women of her own age, which is the correct view. It has been said it means the women of all the worlds until the Day of Resurrection, and al-Zajjaj chose this view. It has also been said that the second choosing is an emphasis of the first, and both refer to one thing.

His saying, ﴿O Maryam, be devoted to your Lord﴾: that is, prolong standing in prayer, or be constant. The meanings of *qunut* (*qunut*, "devotion") have already been discussed. He placed prostration before bowing because it is more excellent, or because their prayer had no fixed order, and the *wa* (*wa*, "and") is merely for joining without ordering.

His saying, ﴿and bow with those who bow﴾: its apparent meaning is that her bowing is together with their bowing, which indicates the legislation of congregational prayer. It has also been said that the meaning is that she does the same as their action, even if she did not pray with them. The reference in His saying "dhalika" (*dhalika*, "that") is to what preceded of the matters Allah informed about. Revelation (*wahy*, "revelation") in the language is informing in concealment. It is said: "wahy" and "awha" with the same meaning. Ibn Faris said: revelation is gesture, writing, message, and whatever you cast to another until you inform him.

His saying, ﴿And you were not with them﴾: that is, you were not present with them, meaning those who disputed over the upbringing of Maryam. He negated his presence with them even though it was known, because they denied the revelation. If that denial had been valid, there would have remained no way to know it except by witnessing and presence, and they do not claim that. Thus it is established that it was revelation, along with their acknowledgment that he was not one who reads the Torah nor one who associates with its people. "Al-aqlam" (*al-aqlam*, "the pens") is the plural of "qalam" (*qalam*, "pen"), from *qalamahu* when he cut it, meaning: pens with which they write. It has also been said they are arrows used for drawing lots. ﴿Which of them would take charge of Maryam﴾: that is, nurse her, meaning: they cast their pens to know which of them would take charge of her. This occurred during their dispute over her guardianship. Zakariyya said: he has the most right to her, since her maternal aunt was with him, and she was Ash'a, the sister of Hannah, the mother of Maryam. The children of Israel said: we have the most right to her, since she is the daughter of our scholar. So they drew lots and placed their pens in the flowing water, on the basis that whoever's pen stood still and did not flow with the water would be her guardian. Their pens flowed, and Zakariyya's pen stood still. Those who affirm the drawing of lots have used this as evidence, and the disagreement regarding that is well known. Authentic hadiths have been established regarding its validity.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: when Zakariyya saw that, meaning summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer with Maryam, he said: "Indeed the One who brought this to Maryam out of its season is able to grant me a child." That was when he called upon his Lord. Ibn 'Asakir related similarly from al-Hasan. Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi regarding ﴿good offspring﴾, that he said: "blessed."

Ibn Jarir related from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad, who said: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "Then Jibril called him while he was standing and praying in the niche." Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi that he said: ﴿Then the angels called him﴾ means Jibril. Ibn al-Mundhir related from al-Suddi, who said: "al-mihrab" (*al-mihrab*, "the niche") is the place of prayer. Al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn 'Umar that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of these altars," meaning the sanctuaries (*al-mahareeb*). Ibn Abi Shaybah related in al-Musannaf from Musa al-Juhani, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My community will remain in goodness as long as they do not take altars in their mosques like the altars of the Christians."

It has been related that the disapproval of this (naming him Yahya) was reported from a group of the Companions. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah that he said: "He was named Yaḥyā only because Allah gave him life (aḥyāhu) through faith."

They also related from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾, that he said: "ʿĪsā ibn Maryam is the Word."

Ibn Jarīr related through the route of Ibn Jurayj from him, who said: "Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā were cousins on the mother's side. Yaḥyā's mother used to say to Maryam: 'I find that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb.' That is his confirmation of ʿĪsā, his prostration in his mother's womb, and he was the first to confirm ʿĪsā."

Aḥmad, in the *Kitāb al-Zuhd* (the Book of Asceticism), and Ibn Jarīr related a similar report from Mujāhid. Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿and a master﴾ that he said: "forbearing and pious." ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid that he said: "al-sayyid is the one noble before Allah." Ibn Jarīr related from Ibn al-Musayyab that he said: "al-sayyid is the jurist, the learned."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying ﴿and a master and chaste﴾, that he said: "al-sayyid is the forbearing, and al-ḥaṣūr is the one who does not approach women." Aḥmad in the *Zuhd* related the same from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning al-ḥaṣūr. Aḥmad in the *Zuhd*, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "al-ḥaṣūr is the one who does not emit semen (lā yunzilu al-māʾ)." Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "His member was like the fringe of a garment (hudbat al-thawb)."

Ibn Abī Shaybah and Aḥmad in the *Zuhd* related it by another route from Ibn ʿAmr as a statement of his own (mawqūfan), and this is stronger.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Shuʿayb al-Jubbāʾī that he said: "The name of Yaḥyā's mother was Ashyaʿ." Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj concerning His saying ﴿Make for me a sign﴾ that he said: "By the conception of him (al-ḥaml bihi)."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah concerning His saying ﴿He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days"﴾ that he said: "He was punished with this only because the angels addressed him directly (shāfahat) with this, giving him good news of Yaḥyā. So he asked for the sign after the angels' speech to him, and so his tongue was restrained."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying ﴿except by gesture (ramzan)﴾ that he said: "The ramz is with the two lips." ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related the same from Mujāhid. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he said: "The ramz is signalling (al-ishārah)."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning (bi-l-ʿashiyyi wa-l-ibkār)﴾ that he said: "al-ʿashiyy is the sun's inclining until it sets, and al-ibkār is the beginning of dawn."

It is established in the two *Ṣaḥīḥs* (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and others, from the hadith of ʿAlī, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The best of its women is Maryam bint ʿImrān, and the best of its women is Khadījah bint Khuwaylid.'" al-Ḥākim related and authenticated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The best of the women of the worlds are Khadījah, Fāṭimah, Maryam and Āsiyah the wife of Pharaoh.'" Ibn Mardawayh related a similar report from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī (who authenticated it), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Ḥibbān and al-Ḥākim related a similar report from the hadith of Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). In the two *Ṣaḥīḥs* and others, from the hadith of Abū Mūsā, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Many men have become perfect, but among women none has become perfect except Maryam bint ʿImrān and Āsiyah the wife of Pharaoh. And the excellence of ʿĀʾishah over women is like the excellence of tharīd over (other) food.'"

There are many hadiths with this meaning, and all of them indicate that Maryam (peace be upon her) is the mistress of the women of her own world, not of the women of all the worlds. This is supported by what Ibn ʿAsākir related from Muqātil, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Four women are the mistresses of the women of their worlds: Maryam bint ʿImrān, Āsiyah bint Muzāḥim, Khadījah bint Khuwaylid, and Fāṭimah bint Muḥammad, and the most excellent of them in knowledge is Fāṭimah."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾ that he said: "Prolong the rukūd, meaning the standing (al-qiyām)." Ibn Jarīr related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning ﴿be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾ that he said: "Be sincere." He also related from Qatādah that he said: "Obey your Lord."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related through the route of al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens﴾ that he said: "When Maryam was placed in the mosque, the people of the place of prayer (ahl al-muṣallā), who were writing down the revelation, drew lots over her, casting their pens to determine which of them would take charge of her. Allah said to Muḥammad ﴿And you were not with them﴾, and so on." Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿIkrimah that he said: "They cast their pens into the water, and they went with the current, and the pen of Zakariyyā rose up, so Zakariyyā took charge of her." Ibn Jarīr related a similar report from al-Rabīʿ.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd related from Mujāhid, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim likewise related from Ibn Jurayj, that the pens were those with which they wrote the Torah. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿAṭāʾ that they were the arrows (al-qidāḥ, used for divination).

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 3, verses 38–44 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, "hunalika" (*hunalika*, "at that place/time") is an adverbial expression used for both time and place. Its original use is for place. It has been said that it is used for time specifically, while *hunaka* (*hunaka*, "there") is for place. It has also been said that each of the two may be used in place of the other. The *lam* indicates distance, and the *kaf* indicates address.

The meaning is that he (Zakariyya) made his supplication in that place where he was standing, next to Maryam, or at that time, asking Allah to grant him good offspring. What prompted him to this was what he saw of Hannah's bearing of Maryam, although she had been barren. Thus he gained hope of a child, even though he was old and his wife was barren. Or what prompted him to this was what he saw of winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter with Maryam, because whoever brings that about out of its season is able to bring about a child from a barren woman. On this view, this statement is a new narrative inserted within the story of Maryam because of the connection between them. *Dhurriyyah* (*dhurriyyah*, "offspring") and *nasl* (*nasl*, "progeny") may be used for the singular and for the plural, and the text indicates that it is singular here. His saying, ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir﴾, uses "waliyyan" (*waliyyan*, "an heir") and not "awliya'" (*awliya'*, "heirs"). The feminine form of "tayyibah" (*tayyibah*, "good") is because the word "dhurriyyah" is feminine.

His saying, ﴿Then the angels called him﴾: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "fa-nadahu" (*fa-nadahu*, "then he called him"), and Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud also read it this way. The rest read ﴿fa-nadathu al-malaikah﴾ (*fa-nadathu al-malaikah*, "then the angels called him"). It has been said that the intended one here is Jibril (Gabriel), and that using a plural form for a singular is permissible in Arabic. Among its examples is ﴿those to whom the people said﴾ [Al 'Imran: 173]. It has also been said that all of the angels called him, and this is the apparent meaning from attributing the verb to a plural. The literal meaning takes precedence, so one does not turn to a metaphorical meaning except with an indicator.

His saying, "wa-huwa qa'im" (*wa-huwa qa'im*, "while he was standing"), is a circumstantial clause (*jumlah haliyyah*). ﴿Praying in the niche﴾ is either a description of "qa'im" or a second predicate of "wa-huwa."

His saying, ﴿that Allah gives you good news﴾: it is read with the *fath* on *anna* (*anna*, "that"), with the implied meaning "bi-anna Allah" (*bi-anna Allah*, "that Allah"). It is also read with the *kasrah* on it, as if there were an implied verb of saying. The people of Medina read "yubashshiruka" (*yubashshiruka*, "gives you good news") with the doubled letter (shaddah). Hamzah read it with the lightened form. Humayd ibn Qays al-Makki read it with the *kasrah* and the *dammah* on the present-tense prefix letter.

Al-Akhfash said: these are three dialects with one meaning. The first reading is the one that occurs frequently in the Qur'an, such as ﴿So give good news to My servants﴾ [al-Zumar: 17], ﴿So give him good news of forgiveness﴾ [Ya-Sin: 11], ﴿So We gave her good news of Ishaq﴾ [Hud: 71], and ﴿They said: We give you good news of the truth﴾ [al-Hijr: 55]. This is the reading of the majority. The second is the dialect of the people of Tihamah, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud also read in this way. The third is from *abshara yubshiru ibsharan* (*abshara yubshiru ibshaaran*).

"Yahya" (*Yahya*) cannot take nunation, either because it is non-Arabic or because it has the form of a verb, like "ya'mar," together with being a proper name.

Al-Qurtubi, quoting from al-Naqqash, said: his name in the earlier Book was "Hanna," and that is the end of the quotation. What we have seen in several places in the Gospel is that his name is "Yuhanna" (John). It has been said that he was so named because Allah gave him life through faith and prophethood. It has also been said that he was so named because Allah gave life to people through him with guidance. The meaning here is the announcement of his birth, that is, "He gives you good news of the birth of Yahya."

His saying, ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾, means with 'Isa (peace be upon him). He was called "the word of Allah" because he came into being by the saying of the Exalted: "Be!" It has also been said that he was called "the word of Allah" because people are guided by him just as they are guided by the speech of Allah.

Abu 'Ubayd said: the meaning of ﴿a word from Allah﴾ is "a book from Allah." He said: the Arabs say, "He recited to me his *kalimah*," meaning his poem, just as it is narrated that al-Huwaydirah was mentioned to Hassan, and he said: "May Allah curse his *kalimah*," meaning his poem. That is the end of the quotation.

Yahya was the first to believe in and confirm 'Isa, and he was older than 'Isa by three years. It has also been said by six months. "Sayyid" (*sayyid*, "a leader") is one who leads his people. Al-Zajjaj said: the *sayyid* is one who surpasses his peers in every kind of goodness. "Haswur" (*haswur*, "one who restrains himself") is originally from *hasr*, which means confinement. It is said: "*hasarani al-shay'*" and "*ahsarani*" when a thing confines me. From this is the saying of the poet:

Nor is the separation from Layla that she has drifted away from you,
Nor that preoccupations have confined you.

A "hasur" is one who does not approach women, as if he withholds himself from them. It is said: "a man is *hasur* and *hasir*" when he withholds his gift and does not give it out. So Yahya (peace be upon him) was *hasur* from approaching women, that is, he was restrained and did not approach them as other men do, either because he lacked the ability to do so, or because he restrained himself from them, avoiding desire while having the ability. The second has been preferred, since the context is one of praise, and praise is only for something acquired, which its doer could have done otherwise, not for what is part of one's natural creation and innate disposition.

His saying, ﴿of the righteous﴾: that is, arising from the righteous, because he was from the lineage of the prophets, or being one of the righteous, as in His saying, ﴿and indeed in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah: 130]. Al-Zajjaj said: the righteous one is the one who fulfills to Allah what He has made obligatory upon him, and to people their rights.

His saying, ﴿He said: My Lord, how will I have a boy?﴾: The apparent meaning of this is that the address was from him to Allah, the Exalted, even though the message reaching him came through the angels. This is due to his great humility and eagerness in seeking an answer to his request. It has been said that by "Lord" he meant Jibril, that is, "O my master." It has been said that there are two possible meanings of this question. One is that he asked whether this child would be given to him from his barren wife or from someone else. It has also been said that the meaning is: by what cause do I deserve this, while I and my wife are in this condition? The summary is that he considered the child's coming into being from the two of them unlikely, since custom dictates that such a couple does not produce offspring. This was because on the day of the good news he was old. It has been said he was ninety years old, and it has been said he was a hundred and twenty years old, and his wife was ninety-eight years old. For this reason he said, ﴿And old age has overtaken me﴾, meaning, while this is the case. He made old age like one seeking him, because it is a forerunner of the vanguard of death, so he attributed the verb to it. "Al-'aqir" (*al-'aqir*, "barren") is the one who does not bear children, that is, one who has barrenness by nature. If it had been in the form of a verb, he would have said "'aqirah" (a barren woman in the feminine verbal form), meaning that she has a barrenness that prevents her from having children. This question was asked by him after his supplication that Allah grant him good offspring, and after witnessing that great sign regarding Maryam, as a way of magnifying the power of Allah, the Exalted, and not out of mere disbelief. It has also been said that after his supplication he had waited, until the time that his Lord willed, forty years, and it has been said twenty years. So the astonishment was from this perspective.

His saying, ﴿Thus does Allah do what He wills﴾: that is, Allah does what He wills of wondrous acts like that act, which is bringing forth a child from an old man and a barren woman. The *kaf* (*kaf*, "like") is in the position of an accusative as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, and the demonstrative refers to the verbal noun of "yaf'alu" (*yaf'alu*, "does"). Or the *kaf* is in the position of a nominative as a predicate, meaning: in this wondrous affair, the affair of Allah, and His saying "yaf'alu ma yasha'" (*yaf'alu ma yasha'*, "does what He wills") is an explanation of it. Or the *kaf* is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, meaning: Allah does the act being like that.

His saying, ﴿He said: My Lord, make for me a sign﴾, that is, a sign by which I know the validity of the pregnancy, so that I may receive this blessing with gratitude. ﴿He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture﴾: that is, your sign is that you restrain your tongue from speaking to people for three days, but not from other kinds of remembrance. The reason for making this the sign is so that those days would be devoted to the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, in gratitude for what He bestowed upon him. It has been said that this was a punishment from Allah, the Exalted, upon him, because of his request for a sign after the angels had spoken to him directly. Al-Qurtubi related this from most of the commentators.

"Al-ramz" (*al-ramz*, "gesture") in the language means signaling with the two lips, or the two eyes, or the two eyebrows, or the two hands. Its origin is movement. This is an exception of disjunction (*istithna' munqati'*), because the gesture is not of the same kind as speech. It has been said that it is a connected exception (*istithna' muttasil*), in the sense that speech is whatever conveys understanding, whether by word, sign, or writing. But this is far-fetched. The correct view is the first, and this is what al-Akhfash and al-Kisa'i said.

His saying, ﴿and glorify [your Lord]﴾: that is, glorify Him in the evening, "al-'ashiyy" (*al-'ashiyy*, "evening"), which is the plural of "'ashiyyah." It has been said that it is singular, and it is from the time the sun declines until it sets. It has been said it is from 'Asr until the passing of the first part of the night, and this is very weak. "Al-ibkar" (*al-ibkar*, "morning") is from the rising of dawn until the time of forenoon. It has been said that the intended meaning of glorification is prayer.

His saying, ﴿When the angels said: O Maryam﴾: the adverbial clause is connected to an omitted element, like the first adverbial clause. ﴿Indeed Allah has chosen you﴾: He selected you and purified you from disbelief, or from defilement, in its general sense. ﴿And chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾. It has been said that this second choosing is other than the first choosing. The first is when He accepted her with a good acceptance, and the second is for the birth of 'Isa. The intended meaning of "the worlds" here has been said to be the women of her own age, which is the correct view. It has been said it means the women of all the worlds until the Day of Resurrection, and al-Zajjaj chose this view. It has also been said that the second choosing is an emphasis of the first, and both refer to one thing.

His saying, ﴿O Maryam, be devoted to your Lord﴾: that is, prolong standing in prayer, or be constant. The meanings of *qunut* (*qunut*, "devotion") have already been discussed. He placed prostration before bowing because it is more excellent, or because their prayer had no fixed order, and the *wa* (*wa*, "and") is merely for joining without ordering.

His saying, ﴿and bow with those who bow﴾: its apparent meaning is that her bowing is together with their bowing, which indicates the legislation of congregational prayer. It has also been said that the meaning is that she does the same as their action, even if she did not pray with them. The reference in His saying "dhalika" (*dhalika*, "that") is to what preceded of the matters Allah informed about. Revelation (*wahy*, "revelation") in the language is informing in concealment. It is said: "wahy" and "awha" with the same meaning. Ibn Faris said: revelation is gesture, writing, message, and whatever you cast to another until you inform him.

His saying, ﴿And you were not with them﴾: that is, you were not present with them, meaning those who disputed over the upbringing of Maryam. He negated his presence with them even though it was known, because they denied the revelation. If that denial had been valid, there would have remained no way to know it except by witnessing and presence, and they do not claim that. Thus it is established that it was revelation, along with their acknowledgment that he was not one who reads the Torah nor one who associates with its people. "Al-aqlam" (*al-aqlam*, "the pens") is the plural of "qalam" (*qalam*, "pen"), from *qalamahu* when he cut it, meaning: pens with which they write. It has also been said they are arrows used for drawing lots. ﴿Which of them would take charge of Maryam﴾: that is, nurse her, meaning: they cast their pens to know which of them would take charge of her. This occurred during their dispute over her guardianship. Zakariyya said: he has the most right to her, since her maternal aunt was with him, and she was Ash'a, the sister of Hannah, the mother of Maryam. The children of Israel said: we have the most right to her, since she is the daughter of our scholar. So they drew lots and placed their pens in the flowing water, on the basis that whoever's pen stood still and did not flow with the water would be her guardian. Their pens flowed, and Zakariyya's pen stood still. Those who affirm the drawing of lots have used this as evidence, and the disagreement regarding that is well known. Authentic hadiths have been established regarding its validity.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: when Zakariyya saw that, meaning summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer with Maryam, he said: "Indeed the One who brought this to Maryam out of its season is able to grant me a child." That was when he called upon his Lord. Ibn 'Asakir related similarly from al-Hasan. Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi regarding ﴿good offspring﴾, that he said: "blessed."

Ibn Jarir related from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad, who said: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "Then Jibril called him while he was standing and praying in the niche." Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi that he said: ﴿Then the angels called him﴾ means Jibril. Ibn al-Mundhir related from al-Suddi, who said: "al-mihrab" (*al-mihrab*, "the niche") is the place of prayer. Al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn 'Umar that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of these altars," meaning the sanctuaries (*al-mahareeb*). Ibn Abi Shaybah related in al-Musannaf from Musa al-Juhani, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My community will remain in goodness as long as they do not take altars in their mosques like the altars of the Christians."

It has been related that the disapproval of this (naming him Yahya) was reported from a group of the Companions. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah that he said: "He was named Yaḥyā only because Allah gave him life (aḥyāhu) through faith."

They also related from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾, that he said: "ʿĪsā ibn Maryam is the Word."

Ibn Jarīr related through the route of Ibn Jurayj from him, who said: "Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā were cousins on the mother's side. Yaḥyā's mother used to say to Maryam: 'I find that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb.' That is his confirmation of ʿĪsā, his prostration in his mother's womb, and he was the first to confirm ʿĪsā."

Aḥmad, in the *Kitāb al-Zuhd* (the Book of Asceticism), and Ibn Jarīr related a similar report from Mujāhid. Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿and a master﴾ that he said: "forbearing and pious." ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid that he said: "al-sayyid is the one noble before Allah." Ibn Jarīr related from Ibn al-Musayyab that he said: "al-sayyid is the jurist, the learned."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying ﴿and a master and chaste﴾, that he said: "al-sayyid is the forbearing, and al-ḥaṣūr is the one who does not approach women." Aḥmad in the *Zuhd* related the same from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning al-ḥaṣūr. Aḥmad in the *Zuhd*, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "al-ḥaṣūr is the one who does not emit semen (lā yunzilu al-māʾ)." Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "His member was like the fringe of a garment (hudbat al-thawb)."

Ibn Abī Shaybah and Aḥmad in the *Zuhd* related it by another route from Ibn ʿAmr as a statement of his own (mawqūfan), and this is stronger.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Shuʿayb al-Jubbāʾī that he said: "The name of Yaḥyā's mother was Ashyaʿ." Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj concerning His saying ﴿Make for me a sign﴾ that he said: "By the conception of him (al-ḥaml bihi)."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah concerning His saying ﴿He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days"﴾ that he said: "He was punished with this only because the angels addressed him directly (shāfahat) with this, giving him good news of Yaḥyā. So he asked for the sign after the angels' speech to him, and so his tongue was restrained."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying ﴿except by gesture (ramzan)﴾ that he said: "The ramz is with the two lips." ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related the same from Mujāhid. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he said: "The ramz is signalling (al-ishārah)."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning (bi-l-ʿashiyyi wa-l-ibkār)﴾ that he said: "al-ʿashiyy is the sun's inclining until it sets, and al-ibkār is the beginning of dawn."

It is established in the two *Ṣaḥīḥs* (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and others, from the hadith of ʿAlī, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The best of its women is Maryam bint ʿImrān, and the best of its women is Khadījah bint Khuwaylid.'" al-Ḥākim related and authenticated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The best of the women of the worlds are Khadījah, Fāṭimah, Maryam and Āsiyah the wife of Pharaoh.'" Ibn Mardawayh related a similar report from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī (who authenticated it), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Ḥibbān and al-Ḥākim related a similar report from the hadith of Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). In the two *Ṣaḥīḥs* and others, from the hadith of Abū Mūsā, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Many men have become perfect, but among women none has become perfect except Maryam bint ʿImrān and Āsiyah the wife of Pharaoh. And the excellence of ʿĀʾishah over women is like the excellence of tharīd over (other) food.'"

There are many hadiths with this meaning, and all of them indicate that Maryam (peace be upon her) is the mistress of the women of her own world, not of the women of all the worlds. This is supported by what Ibn ʿAsākir related from Muqātil, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Four women are the mistresses of the women of their worlds: Maryam bint ʿImrān, Āsiyah bint Muzāḥim, Khadījah bint Khuwaylid, and Fāṭimah bint Muḥammad, and the most excellent of them in knowledge is Fāṭimah."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾ that he said: "Prolong the rukūd, meaning the standing (al-qiyām)." Ibn Jarīr related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning ﴿be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾ that he said: "Be sincere." He also related from Qatādah that he said: "Obey your Lord."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related through the route of al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens﴾ that he said: "When Maryam was placed in the mosque, the people of the place of prayer (ahl al-muṣallā), who were writing down the revelation, drew lots over her, casting their pens to determine which of them would take charge of her. Allah said to Muḥammad ﴿And you were not with them﴾, and so on." Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿIkrimah that he said: "They cast their pens into the water, and they went with the current, and the pen of Zakariyyā rose up, so Zakariyyā took charge of her." Ibn Jarīr related a similar report from al-Rabīʿ.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd related from Mujāhid, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim likewise related from Ibn Jurayj, that the pens were those with which they wrote the Torah. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿAṭāʾ that they were the arrows (al-qidāḥ, used for divination).

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 3, verses 38–44 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, "hunalika" (*hunalika*, "at that place/time") is an adverbial expression used for both time and place. Its original use is for place. It has been said that it is used for time specifically, while *hunaka* (*hunaka*, "there") is for place. It has also been said that each of the two may be used in place of the other. The *lam* indicates distance, and the *kaf* indicates address.

The meaning is that he (Zakariyya) made his supplication in that place where he was standing, next to Maryam, or at that time, asking Allah to grant him good offspring. What prompted him to this was what he saw of Hannah's bearing of Maryam, although she had been barren. Thus he gained hope of a child, even though he was old and his wife was barren. Or what prompted him to this was what he saw of winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter with Maryam, because whoever brings that about out of its season is able to bring about a child from a barren woman. On this view, this statement is a new narrative inserted within the story of Maryam because of the connection between them. *Dhurriyyah* (*dhurriyyah*, "offspring") and *nasl* (*nasl*, "progeny") may be used for the singular and for the plural, and the text indicates that it is singular here. His saying, ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir﴾, uses "waliyyan" (*waliyyan*, "an heir") and not "awliya'" (*awliya'*, "heirs"). The feminine form of "tayyibah" (*tayyibah*, "good") is because the word "dhurriyyah" is feminine.

His saying, ﴿Then the angels called him﴾: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "fa-nadahu" (*fa-nadahu*, "then he called him"), and Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud also read it this way. The rest read ﴿fa-nadathu al-malaikah﴾ (*fa-nadathu al-malaikah*, "then the angels called him"). It has been said that the intended one here is Jibril (Gabriel), and that using a plural form for a singular is permissible in Arabic. Among its examples is ﴿those to whom the people said﴾ [Al 'Imran: 173]. It has also been said that all of the angels called him, and this is the apparent meaning from attributing the verb to a plural. The literal meaning takes precedence, so one does not turn to a metaphorical meaning except with an indicator.

His saying, "wa-huwa qa'im" (*wa-huwa qa'im*, "while he was standing"), is a circumstantial clause (*jumlah haliyyah*). ﴿Praying in the niche﴾ is either a description of "qa'im" or a second predicate of "wa-huwa."

His saying, ﴿that Allah gives you good news﴾: it is read with the *fath* on *anna* (*anna*, "that"), with the implied meaning "bi-anna Allah" (*bi-anna Allah*, "that Allah"). It is also read with the *kasrah* on it, as if there were an implied verb of saying. The people of Medina read "yubashshiruka" (*yubashshiruka*, "gives you good news") with the doubled letter (shaddah). Hamzah read it with the lightened form. Humayd ibn Qays al-Makki read it with the *kasrah* and the *dammah* on the present-tense prefix letter.

Al-Akhfash said: these are three dialects with one meaning. The first reading is the one that occurs frequently in the Qur'an, such as ﴿So give good news to My servants﴾ [al-Zumar: 17], ﴿So give him good news of forgiveness﴾ [Ya-Sin: 11], ﴿So We gave her good news of Ishaq﴾ [Hud: 71], and ﴿They said: We give you good news of the truth﴾ [al-Hijr: 55]. This is the reading of the majority. The second is the dialect of the people of Tihamah, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud also read in this way. The third is from *abshara yubshiru ibsharan* (*abshara yubshiru ibshaaran*).

"Yahya" (*Yahya*) cannot take nunation, either because it is non-Arabic or because it has the form of a verb, like "ya'mar," together with being a proper name.

Al-Qurtubi, quoting from al-Naqqash, said: his name in the earlier Book was "Hanna," and that is the end of the quotation. What we have seen in several places in the Gospel is that his name is "Yuhanna" (John). It has been said that he was so named because Allah gave him life through faith and prophethood. It has also been said that he was so named because Allah gave life to people through him with guidance. The meaning here is the announcement of his birth, that is, "He gives you good news of the birth of Yahya."

His saying, ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾, means with 'Isa (peace be upon him). He was called "the word of Allah" because he came into being by the saying of the Exalted: "Be!" It has also been said that he was called "the word of Allah" because people are guided by him just as they are guided by the speech of Allah.

Abu 'Ubayd said: the meaning of ﴿a word from Allah﴾ is "a book from Allah." He said: the Arabs say, "He recited to me his *kalimah*," meaning his poem, just as it is narrated that al-Huwaydirah was mentioned to Hassan, and he said: "May Allah curse his *kalimah*," meaning his poem. That is the end of the quotation.

Yahya was the first to believe in and confirm 'Isa, and he was older than 'Isa by three years. It has also been said by six months. "Sayyid" (*sayyid*, "a leader") is one who leads his people. Al-Zajjaj said: the *sayyid* is one who surpasses his peers in every kind of goodness. "Haswur" (*haswur*, "one who restrains himself") is originally from *hasr*, which means confinement. It is said: "*hasarani al-shay'*" and "*ahsarani*" when a thing confines me. From this is the saying of the poet:

Nor is the separation from Layla that she has drifted away from you,
Nor that preoccupations have confined you.

A "hasur" is one who does not approach women, as if he withholds himself from them. It is said: "a man is *hasur* and *hasir*" when he withholds his gift and does not give it out. So Yahya (peace be upon him) was *hasur* from approaching women, that is, he was restrained and did not approach them as other men do, either because he lacked the ability to do so, or because he restrained himself from them, avoiding desire while having the ability. The second has been preferred, since the context is one of praise, and praise is only for something acquired, which its doer could have done otherwise, not for what is part of one's natural creation and innate disposition.

His saying, ﴿of the righteous﴾: that is, arising from the righteous, because he was from the lineage of the prophets, or being one of the righteous, as in His saying, ﴿and indeed in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah: 130]. Al-Zajjaj said: the righteous one is the one who fulfills to Allah what He has made obligatory upon him, and to people their rights.

His saying, ﴿He said: My Lord, how will I have a boy?﴾: The apparent meaning of this is that the address was from him to Allah, the Exalted, even though the message reaching him came through the angels. This is due to his great humility and eagerness in seeking an answer to his request. It has been said that by "Lord" he meant Jibril, that is, "O my master." It has been said that there are two possible meanings of this question. One is that he asked whether this child would be given to him from his barren wife or from someone else. It has also been said that the meaning is: by what cause do I deserve this, while I and my wife are in this condition? The summary is that he considered the child's coming into being from the two of them unlikely, since custom dictates that such a couple does not produce offspring. This was because on the day of the good news he was old. It has been said he was ninety years old, and it has been said he was a hundred and twenty years old, and his wife was ninety-eight years old. For this reason he said, ﴿And old age has overtaken me﴾, meaning, while this is the case. He made old age like one seeking him, because it is a forerunner of the vanguard of death, so he attributed the verb to it. "Al-'aqir" (*al-'aqir*, "barren") is the one who does not bear children, that is, one who has barrenness by nature. If it had been in the form of a verb, he would have said "'aqirah" (a barren woman in the feminine verbal form), meaning that she has a barrenness that prevents her from having children. This question was asked by him after his supplication that Allah grant him good offspring, and after witnessing that great sign regarding Maryam, as a way of magnifying the power of Allah, the Exalted, and not out of mere disbelief. It has also been said that after his supplication he had waited, until the time that his Lord willed, forty years, and it has been said twenty years. So the astonishment was from this perspective.

His saying, ﴿Thus does Allah do what He wills﴾: that is, Allah does what He wills of wondrous acts like that act, which is bringing forth a child from an old man and a barren woman. The *kaf* (*kaf*, "like") is in the position of an accusative as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, and the demonstrative refers to the verbal noun of "yaf'alu" (*yaf'alu*, "does"). Or the *kaf* is in the position of a nominative as a predicate, meaning: in this wondrous affair, the affair of Allah, and His saying "yaf'alu ma yasha'" (*yaf'alu ma yasha'*, "does what He wills") is an explanation of it. Or the *kaf* is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, meaning: Allah does the act being like that.

His saying, ﴿He said: My Lord, make for me a sign﴾, that is, a sign by which I know the validity of the pregnancy, so that I may receive this blessing with gratitude. ﴿He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture﴾: that is, your sign is that you restrain your tongue from speaking to people for three days, but not from other kinds of remembrance. The reason for making this the sign is so that those days would be devoted to the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, in gratitude for what He bestowed upon him. It has been said that this was a punishment from Allah, the Exalted, upon him, because of his request for a sign after the angels had spoken to him directly. Al-Qurtubi related this from most of the commentators.

"Al-ramz" (*al-ramz*, "gesture") in the language means signaling with the two lips, or the two eyes, or the two eyebrows, or the two hands. Its origin is movement. This is an exception of disjunction (*istithna' munqati'*), because the gesture is not of the same kind as speech. It has been said that it is a connected exception (*istithna' muttasil*), in the sense that speech is whatever conveys understanding, whether by word, sign, or writing. But this is far-fetched. The correct view is the first, and this is what al-Akhfash and al-Kisa'i said.

His saying, ﴿and glorify [your Lord]﴾: that is, glorify Him in the evening, "al-'ashiyy" (*al-'ashiyy*, "evening"), which is the plural of "'ashiyyah." It has been said that it is singular, and it is from the time the sun declines until it sets. It has been said it is from 'Asr until the passing of the first part of the night, and this is very weak. "Al-ibkar" (*al-ibkar*, "morning") is from the rising of dawn until the time of forenoon. It has been said that the intended meaning of glorification is prayer.

His saying, ﴿When the angels said: O Maryam﴾: the adverbial clause is connected to an omitted element, like the first adverbial clause. ﴿Indeed Allah has chosen you﴾: He selected you and purified you from disbelief, or from defilement, in its general sense. ﴿And chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾. It has been said that this second choosing is other than the first choosing. The first is when He accepted her with a good acceptance, and the second is for the birth of 'Isa. The intended meaning of "the worlds" here has been said to be the women of her own age, which is the correct view. It has been said it means the women of all the worlds until the Day of Resurrection, and al-Zajjaj chose this view. It has also been said that the second choosing is an emphasis of the first, and both refer to one thing.

His saying, ﴿O Maryam, be devoted to your Lord﴾: that is, prolong standing in prayer, or be constant. The meanings of *qunut* (*qunut*, "devotion") have already been discussed. He placed prostration before bowing because it is more excellent, or because their prayer had no fixed order, and the *wa* (*wa*, "and") is merely for joining without ordering.

His saying, ﴿and bow with those who bow﴾: its apparent meaning is that her bowing is together with their bowing, which indicates the legislation of congregational prayer. It has also been said that the meaning is that she does the same as their action, even if she did not pray with them. The reference in His saying "dhalika" (*dhalika*, "that") is to what preceded of the matters Allah informed about. Revelation (*wahy*, "revelation") in the language is informing in concealment. It is said: "wahy" and "awha" with the same meaning. Ibn Faris said: revelation is gesture, writing, message, and whatever you cast to another until you inform him.

His saying, ﴿And you were not with them﴾: that is, you were not present with them, meaning those who disputed over the upbringing of Maryam. He negated his presence with them even though it was known, because they denied the revelation. If that denial had been valid, there would have remained no way to know it except by witnessing and presence, and they do not claim that.
