The *lam* indicates distance, and the *kaf* indicates address.

The meaning is that he (Zakariyya) made his supplication in that place where he was standing, next to Maryam, or at that time, asking Allah to grant him good offspring. What prompted him to this was what he saw of Hannah's bearing of Maryam, although she had been barren. Thus he gained hope of a child, even though he was old and his wife was barren. Or what prompted him to this was what he saw of winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter with Maryam, because whoever brings that about out of its season is able to bring about a child from a barren woman. On this view, this statement is a new narrative inserted within the story of Maryam because of the connection between them. *Dhurriyyah* (*dhurriyyah*, "offspring") and *nasl* (*nasl*, "progeny") may be used for the singular and for the plural, and the text indicates that it is singular here. His saying, ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir﴾, uses "waliyyan" (*waliyyan*, "an heir") and not "awliya'" (*awliya'*, "heirs"). The feminine form of "tayyibah" (*tayyibah*, "good") is because the word "dhurriyyah" is feminine.

His saying, ﴿Then the angels called him﴾: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "fa-nadahu" (*fa-nadahu*, "then he called him"), and Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud also read it this way. The rest read ﴿fa-nadathu al-malaikah﴾ (*fa-nadathu al-malaikah*, "then the angels called him"). It has been said that the intended one here is Jibril (Gabriel), and that using a plural form for a singular is permissible in Arabic. Among its examples is ﴿those to whom the people said﴾ [Al 'Imran: 173]. It has also been said that all of the angels called him, and this is the apparent meaning from attributing the verb to a plural. The literal meaning takes precedence, so one does not turn to a metaphorical meaning except with an indicator.

His saying, "wa-huwa qa'im" (*wa-huwa qa'im*, "while he was standing"), is a circumstantial clause (*jumlah haliyyah*). ﴿Praying in the niche﴾ is either a description of "qa'im" or a second predicate of "wa-huwa."

His saying, ﴿that Allah gives you good news﴾: it is read with the *fath* on *anna* (*anna*, "that"), with the implied meaning "bi-anna Allah" (*bi-anna Allah*, "that Allah"). It is also read with the *kasrah* on it, as if there were an implied verb of saying. The people of Medina read "yubashshiruka" (*yubashshiruka*, "gives you good news") with the doubled letter (shaddah). Hamzah read it with the lightened form. Humayd ibn Qays al-Makki read it with the *kasrah* and the *dammah* on the present-tense prefix letter.

Al-Akhfash said: these are three dialects with one meaning. The first reading is the one that occurs frequently in the Qur'an, such as ﴿So give good news to My servants﴾ [al-Zumar: 17], ﴿So give him good news of forgiveness﴾ [Ya-Sin: 11], ﴿So We gave her good news of Ishaq﴾ [Hud: 71], and ﴿They said: We give you good news of the truth﴾ [al-Hijr: 55]. This is the reading of the majority. The second is the dialect of the people of Tihamah, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud also read in this way. The third is from *abshara yubshiru ibsharan* (*abshara yubshiru ibshaaran*).

"Yahya" (*Yahya*) cannot take nunation, either because it is non-Arabic or because it has the form of a verb, like "ya'mar," together with being a proper name.

Al-Qurtubi, quoting from al-Naqqash, said: his name in the earlier Book was "Hanna," and that is the end of the quotation. What we have seen in several places in the Gospel is that his name is "Yuhanna" (John). It has been said that he was so named because Allah gave him life through faith and prophethood. It has also been said that he was so named because Allah gave life to people through him with guidance. The meaning here is the announcement of his birth, that is, "He gives you good news of the birth of Yahya."

His saying, ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾, means with 'Isa (peace be upon him). He was called "the word of Allah" because he came into being by the saying of the Exalted: "Be!" It has also been said that he was called "the word of Allah" because people are guided by him just as they are guided by the speech of Allah.

Abu 'Ubayd said: the meaning of ﴿a word from Allah﴾ is "a book from Allah." He said: the Arabs say, "He recited to me his *kalimah*," meaning his poem, just as it is narrated that al-Huwaydirah was mentioned to Hassan, and he said: "May Allah curse his *kalimah*," meaning his poem. That is the end of the quotation.

Yahya was the first to believe in and confirm 'Isa, and he was older than 'Isa by three years. It has also been said by six months. "Sayyid" (*sayyid*, "a leader") is one who leads his people. Al-Zajjaj said: the *sayyid* is one who surpasses his peers in every kind of goodness. "Haswur" (*haswur*, "one who restrains himself") is originally from *hasr*, which means confinement. It is said: "*hasarani al-shay'*" and "*ahsarani*" when a thing confines me. From this is the saying of the poet:

Nor is the separation from Layla that she has drifted away from you,
Nor that preoccupations have confined you.

A "hasur" is one who does not approach women, as if he withholds himself from them. It is said: "a man is *hasur* and *hasir*" when he withholds his gift and does not give it out. So Yahya (peace be upon him) was *hasur* from approaching women, that is, he was restrained and did not approach them as other men do, either because he lacked the ability to do so, or because he restrained himself from them, avoiding desire while having the ability. The second has been preferred, since the context is one of praise, and praise is only for something acquired, which its doer could have done otherwise, not for what is part of one's natural creation and innate disposition.

His saying, ﴿of the righteous﴾: that is, arising from the righteous, because he was from the lineage of the prophets, or being one of the righteous, as in His saying, ﴿and indeed in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah: 130]. Al-Zajjaj said: the righteous one is the one who fulfills to Allah what He has made obligatory upon him, and to people their rights.

His saying, ﴿He said: My Lord, how will I have a boy?﴾: The apparent meaning of this is that the address was from him to Allah, the Exalted, even though the message reaching him came through the angels. This is due to his great humility and eagerness in seeking an answer to his request. It has been said that by "Lord" he meant Jibril, that is, "O my master." It has been said that there are two possible meanings of this question. One is that he asked whether this child would be given to him from his barren wife or from someone else. It has also been said that the meaning is: by what cause do I deserve this, while I and my wife are in this condition? The summary is that he considered the child's coming into being from the two of them unlikely, since custom dictates that such a couple does not produce offspring. This was because on the day of the good news he was old. It has been said he was ninety years old, and it has been said he was a hundred and twenty years old, and his wife was ninety-eight years old. For this reason he said, ﴿And old age has overtaken me﴾, meaning, while this is the case. He made old age like one seeking him, because it is a forerunner of the vanguard of death, so he attributed the verb to it. "Al-'aqir" (*al-'aqir*, "barren") is the one who does not bear children, that is, one who has barrenness by nature. If it had been in the form of a verb, he would have said "'aqirah" (a barren woman in the feminine verbal form), meaning that she has a barrenness that prevents her from having children. This question was asked by him after his supplication that Allah grant him good offspring, and after witnessing that great sign regarding Maryam, as a way of magnifying the power of Allah, the Exalted, and not out of mere disbelief. It has also been said that after his supplication he had waited, until the time that his Lord willed, forty years, and it has been said twenty years. So the astonishment was from this perspective.

His saying, ﴿Thus does Allah do what He wills﴾: that is, Allah does what He wills of wondrous acts like that act, which is bringing forth a child from an old man and a barren woman. The *kaf* (*kaf*, "like") is in the position of an accusative as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, and the demonstrative refers to the verbal noun of "yaf'alu" (*yaf'alu*, "does"). Or the *kaf* is in the position of a nominative as a predicate, meaning: in this wondrous affair, the affair of Allah, and His saying "yaf'alu ma yasha'" (*yaf'alu ma yasha'*, "does what He wills") is an explanation of it. Or the *kaf* is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, meaning: Allah does the act being like that.

His saying, ﴿He said: My Lord, make for me a sign﴾, that is, a sign by which I know the validity of the pregnancy, so that I may receive this blessing with gratitude. ﴿He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture﴾: that is, your sign is that you restrain your tongue from speaking to people for three days, but not from other kinds of remembrance. The reason for making this the sign is so that those days would be devoted to the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, in gratitude for what He bestowed upon him. It has been said that this was a punishment from Allah, the Exalted, upon him, because of his request for a sign after the angels had spoken to him directly. Al-Qurtubi related this from most of the commentators.

"Al-ramz" (*al-ramz*, "gesture") in the language means signaling with the two lips, or the two eyes, or the two eyebrows, or the two hands. Its origin is movement. This is an exception of disjunction (*istithna' munqati'*), because the gesture is not of the same kind as speech. It has been said that it is a connected exception (*istithna' muttasil*), in the sense that speech is whatever conveys understanding, whether by word, sign, or writing. But this is far-fetched. The correct view is the first, and this is what al-Akhfash and al-Kisa'i said.

His saying, ﴿and glorify [your Lord]﴾: that is, glorify Him in the evening, "al-'ashiyy" (*al-'ashiyy*, "evening"), which is the plural of "'ashiyyah." It has been said that it is singular, and it is from the time the sun declines until it sets. It has been said it is from 'Asr until the passing of the first part of the night, and this is very weak. "Al-ibkar" (*al-ibkar*, "morning") is from the rising of dawn until the time of forenoon. It has been said that the intended meaning of glorification is prayer.

His saying, ﴿When the angels said: O Maryam﴾: the adverbial clause is connected to an omitted element, like the first adverbial clause. ﴿Indeed Allah has chosen you﴾: He selected you and purified you from disbelief, or from defilement, in its general sense. ﴿And chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾. It has been said that this second choosing is other than the first choosing. The first is when He accepted her with a good acceptance, and the second is for the birth of 'Isa. The intended meaning of "the worlds" here has been said to be the women of her own age, which is the correct view. It has been said it means the women of all the worlds until the Day of Resurrection, and al-Zajjaj chose this view. It has also been said that the second choosing is an emphasis of the first, and both refer to one thing.

His saying, ﴿O Maryam, be devoted to your Lord﴾: that is, prolong standing in prayer, or be constant. The meanings of *qunut* (*qunut*, "devotion") have already been discussed. He placed prostration before bowing because it is more excellent, or because their prayer had no fixed order, and the *wa* (*wa*, "and") is merely for joining without ordering.

His saying, ﴿and bow with those who bow﴾: its apparent meaning is that her bowing is together with their bowing, which indicates the legislation of congregational prayer. It has also been said that the meaning is that she does the same as their action, even if she did not pray with them. The reference in His saying "dhalika" (*dhalika*, "that") is to what preceded of the matters Allah informed about. Revelation (*wahy*, "revelation") in the language is informing in concealment. It is said: "wahy" and "awha" with the same meaning. Ibn Faris said: revelation is gesture, writing, message, and whatever you cast to another until you inform him.

His saying, ﴿And you were not with them﴾: that is, you were not present with them, meaning those who disputed over the upbringing of Maryam. He negated his presence with them even though it was known, because they denied the revelation. If that denial had been valid, there would have remained no way to know it except by witnessing and presence, and they do not claim that. Thus it is established that it was revelation, along with their acknowledgment that he was not one who reads the Torah nor one who associates with its people. "Al-aqlam" (*al-aqlam*, "the pens") is the plural of "qalam" (*qalam*, "pen"), from *qalamahu* when he cut it, meaning: pens with which they write. It has also been said they are arrows used for drawing lots. ﴿Which of them would take charge of Maryam﴾: that is, nurse her, meaning: they cast their pens to know which of them would take charge of her. This occurred during their dispute over her guardianship. Zakariyya said: he has the most right to her, since her maternal aunt was with him, and she was Ash'a, the sister of Hannah, the mother of Maryam. The children of Israel said: we have the most right to her, since she is the daughter of our scholar. So they drew lots and placed their pens in the flowing water, on the basis that whoever's pen stood still and did not flow with the water would be her guardian. Their pens flowed, and Zakariyya's pen stood still. Those who affirm the drawing of lots have used this as evidence, and the disagreement regarding that is well known. Authentic hadiths have been established regarding its validity.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: when Zakariyya saw that, meaning summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer with Maryam, he said: "Indeed the One who brought this to Maryam out of its season is able to grant me a child." That was when he called upon his Lord. Ibn 'Asakir related similarly from al-Hasan. Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi regarding ﴿good offspring﴾, that he said: "blessed."

Ibn Jarir related from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad, who said: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "Then Jibril called him while he was standing and praying in the niche." Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi that he said: ﴿Then the angels called him﴾ means Jibril. Ibn al-Mundhir related from al-Suddi, who said: "al-mihrab" (*al-mihrab*, "the niche") is the place of prayer. Al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn 'Umar that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of these altars," meaning the sanctuaries (*al-mahareeb*). Ibn Abi Shaybah related in al-Musannaf from Musa al-Juhani, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My community will remain in goodness as long as they do not take altars in their mosques like the altars of the Christians."

It has been related that the disapproval of this (naming him Yahya) was reported from a group of the Companions. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah that he said: "He was named Yaḥyā only because Allah gave him life (aḥyāhu) through faith."

They also related from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾, that he said: "ʿĪsā ibn Maryam is the Word."

Ibn Jarīr related through the route of Ibn Jurayj from him, who said: "Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā were cousins on the mother's side. Yaḥyā's mother used to say to Maryam: 'I find that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb.' That is his confirmation of ʿĪsā, his prostration in his mother's womb, and he was the first to confirm ʿĪsā."

Aḥmad, in the *Kitāb al-Zuhd* (the Book of Asceticism), and Ibn Jarīr related a similar report from Mujāhid. Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿and a master﴾ that he said: "forbearing and pious." ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid that he said: "al-sayyid is the one noble before Allah." Ibn Jarīr related from Ibn al-Musayyab that he said: "al-sayyid is the jurist, the learned."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying ﴿and a master and chaste﴾, that he said: "al-sayyid is the forbearing, and al-ḥaṣūr is the one who does not approach women." Aḥmad in the *Zuhd* related the same from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning al-ḥaṣūr. Aḥmad in the *Zuhd*, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "al-ḥaṣūr is the one who does not emit semen (lā yunzilu al-māʾ)." Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "His member was like the fringe of a garment (hudbat al-thawb)."

Ibn Abī Shaybah and Aḥmad in the *Zuhd* related it by another route from Ibn ʿAmr as a statement of his own (mawqūfan), and this is stronger.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Shuʿayb al-Jubbāʾī that he said: "The name of Yaḥyā's mother was Ashyaʿ." Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj concerning His saying ﴿Make for me a sign﴾ that he said: "By the conception of him (al-ḥaml bihi)."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Qatādah concerning His saying ﴿He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days"﴾ that he said: "He was punished with this only because the angels addressed him directly (shāfahat) with this, giving him good news of Yaḥyā. So he asked for the sign after the angels' speech to him, and so his tongue was restrained."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying ﴿except by gesture (ramzan)﴾ that he said: "The ramz is with the two lips." ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related the same from Mujāhid. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he said: "The ramz is signalling (al-ishārah)."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning (bi-l-ʿashiyyi wa-l-ibkār)﴾ that he said: "al-ʿashiyy is the sun's inclining until it sets, and al-ibkār is the beginning of dawn."

It is established in the two *Ṣaḥīḥs* (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and others, from the hadith of ʿAlī, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The best of its women is Maryam bint ʿImrān, and the best of its women is Khadījah bint Khuwaylid.'" al-Ḥākim related and authenticated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The best of the women of the worlds are Khadījah, Fāṭimah, Maryam and Āsiyah the wife of Pharaoh.'" Ibn Mardawayh related a similar report from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī (who authenticated it), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Ḥibbān and al-Ḥākim related a similar report from the hadith of Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). In the two *Ṣaḥīḥs* and others, from the hadith of Abū Mūsā, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Many men have become perfect, but among women none has become perfect except Maryam bint ʿImrān and Āsiyah the wife of Pharaoh. And the excellence of ʿĀʾishah over women is like the excellence of tharīd over (other) food.'"

There are many hadiths with this meaning, and all of them indicate that Maryam (peace be upon her) is the mistress of the women of her own world, not of the women of all the worlds. This is supported by what Ibn ʿAsākir related from Muqātil, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Four women are the mistresses of the women of their worlds: Maryam bint ʿImrān, Āsiyah bint Muzāḥim, Khadījah bint Khuwaylid, and Fāṭimah bint Muḥammad, and the most excellent of them in knowledge is Fāṭimah."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr related from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾ that he said: "Prolong the rukūd, meaning the standing (al-qiyām)." Ibn Jarīr related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning ﴿be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾ that he said: "Be sincere." He also related from Qatādah that he said: "Obey your Lord."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related through the route of al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens﴾ that he said: "When Maryam was placed in the mosque, the people of the place of prayer (ahl al-muṣallā), who were writing down the revelation, drew lots over her, casting their pens to determine which of them would take charge of her. Allah said to Muḥammad ﴿And you were not with them﴾, and so on." Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿIkrimah that he said: "They cast their pens into the water, and they went with the current, and the pen of Zakariyyā rose up, so Zakariyyā took charge of her." Ibn Jarīr related a similar report from al-Rabīʿ.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd related from Mujāhid, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim likewise related from Ibn Jurayj, that the pens were those with which they wrote the Torah. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿAṭāʾ that they were the arrows (al-qidāḥ, used for divination).

His saying, "when the angels said," is a substitute (badal) for his earlier saying "and when the angels said," and what lies between them is a parenthetical clause (i'tirad). It was also said that it is a substitute for "when they dispute" (idh yakhtasimun). It was also said that it is governed (mansub) by a verb that is implied, and it was said that it is governed by his saying "they dispute," and it was said that it is governed by his saying "and you were not with them" (wa ma kunta ladayhim).

Regarding al-Masih (the Messiah), there has been disagreement about what it was derived from. It was said that it derives from al-mash (wiping), because he traveled through the earth (masaha al-ard), that is, he went about in it and did not settle under any shelter. It was also said that he did not wipe anyone afflicted with a defect except that he was healed, so he was called Masih. On these two views, it is of the pattern fa'il in the sense of fa'il (active). It was said that it is because he would anoint with the oil with which the prophets used to be anointed. It was said that it is because he had smooth soles (mamsuh al-akhmasayn), and it was said that it is because beauty wiped him, and it was said that it is because he was wiped clean of sins by purification. On these four views, it is of the pattern fa'il in the sense of maf'ul (passive).

Abu al-Haytham said: al-Masih is the opposite of al-Masikh, with a ritually marked kha (al-khaʾ al-mu'jama). Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-Masih is al-Siddiq (the truthful one).

Abu 'Ubayd said: its origin in Hebrew is mashikha, with two dotted letters, so it was Arabized, just as Musha was Arabized into Musa. As for al-Dajjal (the Antichrist), he was called Masih because one of his eyes is wiped (blind), and it was said: because he wipes the earth, that is, he travels through its lands, except Makkah, al-Madinah and Bayt al-Maqdis.

His saying ʿIsa is either an explanatory apposition ('atf bayan) or a substitute (badal), and it is a non-Arabic name. It was said: it is an Arabic word derived from ʿasa, yaʿusu, when he governed (sasa). Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: it is Arabized from Ayshuʿ, end of quote.

What we have found in the Gospel in several places is that his name is Yashuʿ without a hamza. The reason it is said "son of Maryam," although the address is directed to her, is to alert that he was born without a father, so he was ascribed to his mother. The wajih is the one who possesses wajaha, which is strength and protection. His wajaha in this world is prophethood, and in the Hereafter it is intercession and high rank. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) of "word." If it is indefinite, then it is a qualifier (mawsufa). Likewise his saying "and of those brought near" (wa min al-muqarrabin) is in the accusative position as a state.

Al-Akhfash said: it is conjoined (ma'tuf) to "wajihan."

Al-Mahd is the bed where the infant lies while nursing. Mahhadtu al-amr means: I prepared it and made it ready.

Al-Kahl is the one who is between the age of youth and old age. That is, he speaks to people both while being a suckling in the cradle and while being a kahl (mature man) with revelation and messengership. This was said by al-Zajjaj. Al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: kahlan is conjoined to "wajihan."

Al-Akhfash said: "and of the righteous" (wa min al-salihin) is conjoined to "wajihan"; that is, he is of the righteous servants.

His saying: ﴿How can I have a son?﴾ means: how could this happen, in the manner of ordinary astonishment. ﴿when no man has touched me﴾ is a circumstantial clause (jumla haliyya): that is, and the state is that he is in a condition contrary to the usual condition of having a father. ﴿He said: "Thus God creates what He wills"﴾ is from the speech of God, glorified is He.

The basic meaning of qada' is judgments, and it has been mentioned before. Here it means will (irada); that is, when He wills a matter among the affairs, ﴿then He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ without labor or effort, and this is an image (tamthil) for the perfection of His power.

His saying ﴿and He will teach him the Book﴾: it was said that it is conjoined to "yubashshiruka" (He gives you glad tidings); that is, God gives you glad tidings and God teaches him. It was said that it is conjoined to "yakhluqu" (He creates), that is: and thus God teaches him. Or it is a new independent sentence brought to comfort her heart.

Al-Kitab means writing (al-kitaba). Al-Hikmah means knowledge. It was said that it is refining of character. The accusative of "rasulan" is by implying "and He makes him a messenger," or "and He speaks to them as a messenger," or "and I have sent a messenger." It was also said: it is conjoined to his saying "wajihan," so it is a circumstantial state, because it has the meaning of speech, that is: and speaking. Al-Akhfash said: if you wish, you may make the waw in his saying "wa rasulan" an interpolated waw (waw muqhama), and make "al-rasul" a circumstantial state.

His saying ﴿that I have come to you﴾ is governed by "rasul," because it contains the meaning of speech, as has passed. It was said that its origin is "bi-anni qad ji'tukum," and the preposition was omitted. It was said that it is governed by a hidden verb, that is, "saying that I have come to you." It was said that it is conjoined to the earlier states. His saying "with a sign" (bi-ayah) is in the accusative position as a circumstantial state; that is, clothed with a sign from your Lord.

His saying "that I create" means: I shape and determine. ﴿for you out of clay, like the form of a bird﴾. This clause is a substitute for the first clause, which is ﴿that I have come to you﴾, or a substitute for "sign," or the predicate of an implied subject, that is: it is "that I." It is read with a kasra on the hamza as a resumption (isti'naf). Al-A'raj and Abu Ja'far read "kahay'at al-tayr" with shadda. The kaf in his saying "kahay'at al-tayr" is an adjective of an implied verbal noun (masdar), that is: I create for you a creation, or a thing like the form of a bird.

His saying "then I breathe into it" means: into that creation, or that thing; so the pronoun refers to the kaf in his saying "kahay'at al-tayr." It was said: the pronoun refers to the bird, that is, one individual of it. It was said: it refers to the clay. It was read "fa-yakunu tairan" and "tairan," like tajir and tajr. It was said that he created nothing but the bat, because of the wonders of its craftsmanship.

Indeed, it has a teat, teeth and an ear, it menstruates and becomes pure. It was said that they asked him to create a bat because of the wonders mentioned, and because it flies without feathers, and gives birth as the rest of animals give birth, despite being of the birds, and does not lay eggs as the rest of birds lay eggs. It cannot see in the light of day nor in the darkness of night; it only sees in two hours: one hour after sunset, and one hour after the dawn breaks. It laughs as a human laughs. It was said that their question to him was in the manner of provocation. It was said that it would fly as long as the people were looking at it, and when it disappeared from their eyes it fell dead, so that the act of God would be distinguished from the act of others.

His saying "by God's permission" contains evidence that, without permission from God, mighty and majestic, he would not have been able to do that, and that the creation of that was by the act of God, glorified is He, which He caused to happen through the hand of ʿIsa, peace be upon him. It was said: the shaping of the clay and the breathing were from ʿIsa, and the creating was from God, mighty and majestic.

His saying ﴿and I heal the blind-born﴾: al-akmah is one who is born blind. So said Abu ʿUbayda. Ibn Faris said: al-kamah is blindness with which a person is born, and it may also occur later. It is said: kamiha yakmahu kamahan, when he became blind, and kamihtu aynahu, when I made his eye blind. It was also said: al-akmah is one who sees by day and does not see by night. It was also said: he is one whose eye has been wiped.

Al-Baras is well known, and it is a whiteness that appears in the skin. ʿIsa, peace be upon him, used to heal many diseases, as the Gospel contains. God, glorified is He, specifically mentioned these two diseases because they generally are not cured by treatment. Likewise the raising of the dead: the Gospel contains stories of that.

The basic meaning of qada' is judgments, and it has been mentioned before. Here it means will (irada); that is, when He wills a matter among the affairs, ﴿then He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ without labor or effort, and this is an image (tamthil) for the perfection of His power.

His saying ﴿and He will teach him the Book﴾: it was said that it is conjoined to "yubashshiruka" (He gives you glad tidings); that is, God gives you glad tidings and God teaches him. It was said that it is conjoined to "yakhluqu" (He creates), that is: and thus God teaches him. Or it is a new independent sentence brought to comfort her heart.

Al-Kitab means writing (al-kitaba). Al-Hikmah means knowledge. It was said that it is refining of character. The accusative of "rasulan" is by implying "and He makes him a messenger," or "and He speaks to them as a messenger," or "and I have sent a messenger." It was also said: it is conjoined to his saying "wajihan," so it is a circumstantial state, because it has the meaning of speech, that is: and speaking. Al-Akhfash said: if you wish, you may make the waw in his saying "wa rasulan" an interpolated waw (waw muqhama), and make "al-rasul" a circumstantial state.

It was said that its origin is "bi-anni qad ji'tukum," and the preposition was omitted. It was said that it is governed by a hidden verb, that is, "saying that I have come to you." It was said that it is conjoined to the earlier states. His saying "with a sign" (bi-ayah) is in the accusative position as a circumstantial state; that is, clothed with a sign from your Lord.

It was said: the pronoun refers to the bird, that is, one individual of it. It was said: it refers to the clay. It was read "fa-yakunu tairan" and "tairan," like tajir and tajr. It was said that he created nothing but the bat, because of the wonders of its craftsmanship.

It was said that their question to him was in the manner of provocation. It was said that it would fly as long as the people were looking at it, and when it disappeared from their eyes it fell dead, so that the act of God would be distinguished from the act of others.

It was said: the shaping of the clay and the breathing were from ʿIsa, and the creating was from God, mighty and majestic.

It was said that it is conjoined to "yakhluqu" (He creates), that is: and thus God teaches him. Or it is a new independent sentence brought to comfort her heart.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Wahb that Jesus was upon the law of Moses, and he observed the Sabbath and faced Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House in Jerusalem). He said to the Children of Israel: "I have not called you to oppose a single letter of what is in the Torah, except that I might make lawful for you some of what was made unlawful for you, and remove from you some of the burdens (al-aṣar)."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Rabi' concerning the verse, who said: "What Jesus brought was gentler than what Moses brought. What had been made unlawful for them in what Moses brought were camel meat and the fat (al-thurub). He made them lawful for them through the tongue of Jesus. He also made unlawful for them the fats (al-shuhum), and they were made lawful for them in what Jesus brought. And [he made lawful] some kinds of fish, some kinds of birds, and other things that he (God) had made unlawful for them and had made stringent upon them in them. Jesus brought them the relaxation of that in the Gospel (al-Injil)."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatadah the like of this.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord﴾, that he said: "It is what Jesus made clear to them of all things, and what his Lord had given him."

His saying, "when the angels said," is a substitute (badal) for his earlier saying "and when the angels said," and what lies between them is a parenthetical clause (i'tirad). It was also said that it is a substitute for "when they dispute" (idh yakhtasimun). It was also said that it is governed (mansub) by a verb that is implied, and it was said that it is governed by his saying "they dispute," and it was said that it is governed by his saying "and you were not with them" (wa ma kunta ladayhim).

Regarding al-Masih (the Messiah), there has been disagreement about what it was derived from. It was said that it derives from al-mash (wiping), because he traveled through the earth (masaha al-ard), that is, he went about in it and did not settle under any shelter. It was also said that he did not wipe anyone afflicted with a defect except that he was healed, so he was called Masih. On these two views, it is of the pattern fa'il in the sense of fa'il (active). It was said that it is because he would anoint with the oil with which the prophets used to be anointed. It was said that it is because he had smooth soles (mamsuh al-akhmasayn), and it was said that it is because beauty wiped him, and it was said that it is because he was wiped clean of sins by purification. On these four views, it is of the pattern fa'il in the sense of maf'ul (passive).

Abu al-Haytham said: al-Masih is the opposite of al-Masikh, with a ritually marked kha (al-khaʾ al-mu'jama). Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-Masih is al-Siddiq (the truthful one).

Abu 'Ubayd said: its origin in Hebrew is mashikha, with two dotted letters, so it was Arabized, just as Musha was Arabized into Musa. As for al-Dajjal (the Antichrist), he was called Masih because one of his eyes is wiped (blind), and it was said: because he wipes the earth, that is, he travels through its lands, except Makkah, al-Madinah and Bayt al-Maqdis.

His saying ʿIsa is either an explanatory apposition ('atf bayan) or a substitute (badal), and it is a non-Arabic name. It was said: it is an Arabic word derived from ʿasa, yaʿusu, when he governed (sasa). Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: it is Arabized from Ayshuʿ, end of quote.

What we have found in the Gospel in several places is that his name is Yashuʿ without a hamza. The reason it is said "son of Maryam," although the address is directed to her, is to alert that he was born without a father, so he was ascribed to his mother. The wajih is the one who possesses wajaha, which is strength and protection. His wajaha in this world is prophethood, and in the Hereafter it is intercession and high rank. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) of "word." If it is indefinite, then it is a qualifier (mawsufa). Likewise his saying "and of those brought near" (wa min al-muqarrabin) is in the accusative position as a state.

Al-Akhfash said: it is conjoined (ma'tuf) to "wajihan."

Al-Mahd is the bed where the infant lies while nursing. Mahhadtu al-amr means: I prepared it and made it ready.

Al-Kahl is the one who is between the age of youth and old age. That is, he speaks to people both while being a suckling in the cradle and while being a kahl (mature man) with revelation and messengership. This was said by al-Zajjaj. Al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: kahlan is conjoined to "wajihan."

Al-Akhfash said: "and of the righteous" (wa min al-salihin) is conjoined to "wajihan"; that is, he is of the righteous servants.

His saying: ﴿How can I have a son?﴾ means: how could this happen, in the manner of ordinary astonishment. ﴿when no man has touched me﴾ is a circumstantial clause (jumla haliyya): that is, and the state is that he is in a condition contrary to the usual condition of having a father. ﴿He said: "Thus God creates what He wills"﴾ is from the speech of God, glorified is He.

The basic meaning of qada' is judgments, and it has been mentioned before. Here it means will (irada); that is, when He wills a matter among the affairs, ﴿then He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ without labor or effort, and this is an image (tamthil) for the perfection of His power.

His saying ﴿and He will teach him the Book﴾: it was said that it is conjoined to "yubashshiruka" (He gives you glad tidings); that is, God gives you glad tidings and God teaches him. It was said that it is conjoined to "yakhluqu" (He creates), that is: and thus God teaches him. Or it is a new independent sentence brought to comfort her heart.

Al-Kitab means writing (al-kitaba). Al-Hikmah means knowledge. It was said that it is refining of character. The accusative of "rasulan" is by implying "and He makes him a messenger," or "and He speaks to them as a messenger," or "and I have sent a messenger." It was also said: it is conjoined to his saying "wajihan," so it is a circumstantial state, because it has the meaning of speech, that is: and speaking. Al-Akhfash said: if you wish, you may make the waw in his saying "wa rasulan" an interpolated waw (waw muqhama), and make "al-rasul" a circumstantial state.

His saying ﴿that I have come to you﴾ is governed by "rasul," because it contains the meaning of speech, as has passed. It was said that its origin is "bi-anni qad ji'tukum," and the preposition was omitted. It was said that it is governed by a hidden verb, that is, "saying that I have come to you." It was said that it is conjoined to the earlier states. His saying "with a sign" (bi-ayah) is in the accusative position as a circumstantial state; that is, clothed with a sign from your Lord.

His saying "that I create" means: I shape and determine. ﴿for you out of clay, like the form of a bird﴾. This clause is a substitute for the first clause, which is ﴿that I have come to you﴾, or a substitute for "sign," or the predicate of an implied subject, that is: it is "that I." It is read with a kasra on the hamza as a resumption (isti'naf). Al-A'raj and Abu Ja'far read "kahay'at al-tayr" with shadda. The kaf in his saying "kahay'at al-tayr" is an adjective of an implied verbal noun (masdar), that is: I create for you a creation, or a thing like the form of a bird.

His saying "then I breathe into it" means: into that creation, or that thing; so the pronoun refers to the kaf in his saying "kahay'at al-tayr." It was said: the pronoun refers to the bird, that is, one individual of it. It was said: it refers to the clay. It was read "fa-yakunu tairan" and "tairan," like tajir and tajr. It was said that he created nothing but the bat, because of the wonders of its craftsmanship.

Indeed, it has a teat, teeth and an ear, it menstruates and becomes pure. It was said that they asked him to create a bat because of the wonders mentioned, and because it flies without feathers, and gives birth as the rest of animals give birth, despite being of the birds, and does not lay eggs as the rest of birds lay eggs. It cannot see in the light of day nor in the darkness of night; it only sees in two hours: one hour after sunset, and one hour after the dawn breaks. It laughs as a human laughs. It was said that their question to him was in the manner of provocation. It was said that it would fly as long as the people were looking at it, and when it disappeared from their eyes it fell dead, so that the act of God would be distinguished from the act of others.

His saying "by God's permission" contains evidence that, without permission from God, mighty and majestic, he would not have been able to do that, and that the creation of that was by the act of God, glorified is He, which He caused to happen through the hand of ʿIsa, peace be upon him. It was said: the shaping of the clay and the breathing were from ʿIsa, and the creating was from God, mighty and majestic.

His saying ﴿and I heal the blind-born﴾: al-akmah is one who is born blind. So said Abu ʿUbayda. Ibn Faris said: al-kamah is blindness with which a person is born, and it may also occur later. It is said: kamiha yakmahu kamahan, when he became blind, and kamihtu aynahu, when I made his eye blind. It was also said: al-akmah is one who sees by day and does not see by night. It was also said: he is one whose eye has been wiped.

Al-Baras is well known, and it is a whiteness that appears in the skin. ʿIsa, peace be upon him, used to heal many diseases, as the Gospel contains. God, glorified is He, specifically mentioned these two diseases because they generally are not cured by treatment. Likewise the raising of the dead: the Gospel contains stories of that.

His saying ﴿and I inform you of what you eat﴾: that is, I tell you of what you eat and of what you store. His saying "wa musaddiqan" (confirming) is conjoined to his saying "wa rasulan." It was also said: the meaning is "and I have come to you confirming."

His saying "wa li-uhilla" means: and in order that I make lawful; that is, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, and I have come to you to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you of foods in the Torah, such as fats and every animal with claws. It was said: he only made lawful for them what the rabbis had forbidden them and what the Torah had not forbidden. Abu ʿUbayda said: it is possible that "baʿd" (some) has the meaning of "kull" (all), and he recited:

"Tarrak amkinatin idha lam arduha aw yartabit baʿd al-nufus himamuha"

Al-Qurtubi said: this view is an error according to the people of reasoning among the linguists, because "baʿd" and "juz'" do not mean "kull," and because ʿIsa did not make lawful for them all that the Torah had forbidden them. He did not make lawful killing, nor theft, nor adultery, nor other forbidden things established in the Gospel while they are also established in the Torah. These are many, as whoever knows both books recognizes. However, "baʿd" may take the place of "kull" with a clear context, like the poet's saying:

"Aba Mundhir afnayta fa-istabqi baʿdana * hanaynaka baʿd al-sharr ahwan min baʿd"

That is: "some of evil is easier than some of it," meaning: some of the evil is easier than all of it.

His saying ﴿with a sign from your Lord﴾: it is his saying ﴿Indeed God is my Lord and your Lord﴾. This was a sign because those prophets before him used to say that, so his coming with what the messengers had brought is a mark of his prophethood. It is possible that this is the earlier sign, so it is a repetition of his saying ﴿that I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, that I create for you from clay﴾, and so on.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding his saying "with a word" (bi-kalima) that he said: ʿIsa is the Word from God.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: al-mahd is the bed of the infant during nursing. It is established in the Sahih that only three spoke in the cradle: ʿIsa; and there was a man among the Children of Israel called Jurayj, who used to pray. His mother came to him and called him, and he said: "Shall I answer her or pray?" She said: "O God, do not let him die until You show him the faces of the prostitutes." Jurayj was in a hermitage, and a woman approached him and spoke to him, but he refused. So she went to a shepherd and let him have her, and she bore a boy and said: "From Jurayj." So they came to him, broke his hermitage, brought him down and insulted him. He performed ablution and prayed, then came to the boy and said: "Who is your father, boy?" He said: "The shepherd." They said: "Shall we build your hermitage of gold?" He said: "No, only of clay." There was a woman of the Children of Israel who was nursing her son, and a rider passed by her, well-dressed, and she said: "O God, make my son like him." So he left her breast and turned to the rider and said: "O God, do not make me like him." Then he turned back to her breast and sucked. Then a slave girl passed by, being dragged and played with, and she said: "O God, do not make my son like this." So he left her breast and said: "O God, make me like her." She said: "Why is that?" He said: "The rider is a tyrant among tyrants, and this slave girl, they say to her: you committed adultery, and she says: God is sufficient for me and He is the best Disposer. And they say: you stole, and she says: God is sufficient for me."

Abu al-Shaykh and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "None spoke in the cradle except ʿIsa, and the witness of Yusuf, and the companion of Jurayj, and the son of Pharaoh's hairdresser."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir transmitted from Qatada regarding his saying ﴿and he speaks to people in the cradle and in maturity﴾ that he said: he speaks to them as a child and as an adult. Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: al-kahl is one who is in the age of kuhula (maturity).

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Mujahid who said: al-kahl is the forbearing one. Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding his saying ﴿and He will teach him the Book﴾ that he said: writing with the pen.

Ibn Jarir transmitted something similar from Ibn Jurayj. Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: ʿIsa created only one bird, and it is the bat.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted through al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: al-akmah is the one born blind. Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him who said: al-akmah is the blind one whose two eyes have been wiped.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Mujahid who said: al-akmah is the one who sees by day and does not see by night. They also transmitted from ʿIkrima who said: al-akmah is al-A'mash (one with weak sight).

Ahmad in al-Zuhd transmitted from Khalid al-Hadhdha' who said: When ʿIsa ibn Maryam sent out his messengers to revive the dead, he would tell them: "Say such and such. When you find a shuddering and a tear, then call upon God at that moment."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Mujahid regarding his saying ﴿and I inform you of what you eat﴾ that he said: of what you ate yesterday of food and what you hid of it.

This was a sign because those prophets before him used to say that, so his coming with what the messengers had brought is a mark of his prophethood. It is possible that this is the earlier sign, so it is a repetition of his saying ﴿that I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, that I create for you from clay﴾, and so on.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding his saying "with a word" (bi-kalima) that he said: ʿIsa is the Word from God.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: al-mahd is the bed of the infant during nursing. It is established in the Sahih that only three spoke in the cradle: ʿIsa; and there was a man among the Children of Israel called Jurayj, who used to pray. His mother came to him and called him, and he said: "Shall I answer her or pray?" She said: "O God, do not let him die until You show him the faces of the prostitutes." Jurayj was in a hermitage, and a woman approached him and spoke to him, but he refused. So she went to a shepherd and let him have her, and she bore a boy and said: "From Jurayj." So they came to him, broke his hermitage, brought him down and insulted him. He performed ablution and prayed, then came to the boy and said: "Who is your father, boy?" He said: "The shepherd." They said: "Shall we build your hermitage of gold?" He said: "No, only of clay." There was a woman of the Children of Israel who was nursing her son, and a rider passed by her, well-dressed, and she said: "O God, make my son like him." So he left her breast and turned to the rider and said: "O God, do not make me like him." Then he turned back to her breast and sucked. Then a slave girl passed by, being dragged and played with, and she said: "O God, do not make my son like this." So he left her breast and said: "O God, make me like her." She said: "Why is that?" He said: "The rider is a tyrant among tyrants, and this slave girl, they say to her: you committed adultery, and she says: God is sufficient for me and He is the best Disposer. And they say: you stole, and she says: God is sufficient for me."

Abu al-Shaykh and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "None spoke in the cradle except ʿIsa, and the witness of Yusuf, and the companion of Jurayj, and the son of Pharaoh's hairdresser."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 3, verses 45–51 (part 2 of 2):

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: "I will inform you of what you eat from the table (al-ma'idah) and what you store from it. He had taken a covenant from them concerning the table when it was sent down, that they should eat and not store. They ate, stored, and betrayed, so they were transformed into apes and swine."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Wahb that Jesus was upon the law of Moses, and he observed the Sabbath and faced Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House in Jerusalem). He said to the Children of Israel: "I have not called you to oppose a single letter of what is in the Torah, except that I might make lawful for you some of what was made unlawful for you, and remove from you some of the burdens (al-aṣar)."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Rabi' concerning the verse, who said: "What Jesus brought was gentler than what Moses brought. What had been made unlawful for them in what Moses brought were camel meat and the fat (al-thurub). He made them lawful for them through the tongue of Jesus. He also made unlawful for them the fats (al-shuhum), and they were made lawful for them in what Jesus brought. And [he made lawful] some kinds of fish, some kinds of birds, and other things that he (God) had made unlawful for them and had made stringent upon them in them. Jesus brought them the relaxation of that in the Gospel (al-Injil)."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatadah the like of this.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord﴾, that he said: "It is what Jesus made clear to them of all things, and what his Lord had given him."

His saying, "when the angels said," is a substitute (badal) for his earlier saying "and when the angels said," and what lies between them is a parenthetical clause (i'tirad). It was also said that it is a substitute for "when they dispute" (idh yakhtasimun). It was also said that it is governed (mansub) by a verb that is implied, and it was said that it is governed by his saying "they dispute," and it was said that it is governed by his saying "and you were not with them" (wa ma kunta ladayhim).

Regarding al-Masih (the Messiah), there has been disagreement about what it was derived from. It was said that it derives from al-mash (wiping), because he traveled through the earth (masaha al-ard), that is, he went about in it and did not settle under any shelter. It was also said that he did not wipe anyone afflicted with a defect except that he was healed, so he was called Masih. On these two views, it is of the pattern fa'il in the sense of fa'il (active). It was said that it is because he would anoint with the oil with which the prophets used to be anointed. It was said that it is because he had smooth soles (mamsuh al-akhmasayn), and it was said that it is because beauty wiped him, and it was said that it is because he was wiped clean of sins by purification. On these four views, it is of the pattern fa'il in the sense of maf'ul (passive).

Abu al-Haytham said: al-Masih is the opposite of al-Masikh, with a ritually marked kha (al-khaʾ al-mu'jama). Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-Masih is al-Siddiq (the truthful one).

Abu 'Ubayd said: its origin in Hebrew is mashikha, with two dotted letters, so it was Arabized, just as Musha was Arabized into Musa. As for al-Dajjal (the Antichrist), he was called Masih because one of his eyes is wiped (blind), and it was said: because he wipes the earth, that is, he travels through its lands, except Makkah, al-Madinah and Bayt al-Maqdis.

His saying ʿIsa is either an explanatory apposition ('atf bayan) or a substitute (badal), and it is a non-Arabic name. It was said: it is an Arabic word derived from ʿasa, yaʿusu, when he governed (sasa). Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: it is Arabized from Ayshuʿ, end of quote.

What we have found in the Gospel in several places is that his name is Yashuʿ without a hamza. The reason it is said "son of Maryam," although the address is directed to her, is to alert that he was born without a father, so he was ascribed to his mother. The wajih is the one who possesses wajaha, which is strength and protection. His wajaha in this world is prophethood, and in the Hereafter it is intercession and high rank. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) of "word." If it is indefinite, then it is a qualifier (mawsufa). Likewise his saying "and of those brought near" (wa min al-muqarrabin) is in the accusative position as a state.

Al-Akhfash said: it is conjoined (ma'tuf) to "wajihan."

Al-Mahd is the bed where the infant lies while nursing. Mahhadtu al-amr means: I prepared it and made it ready.

Al-Kahl is the one who is between the age of youth and old age. That is, he speaks to people both while being a suckling in the cradle and while being a kahl (mature man) with revelation and messengership. This was said by al-Zajjaj. Al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: kahlan is conjoined to "wajihan."

Al-Akhfash said: "and of the righteous" (wa min al-salihin) is conjoined to "wajihan"; that is, he is of the righteous servants.

His saying: ﴿How can I have a son?﴾ means: how could this happen, in the manner of ordinary astonishment. ﴿when no man has touched me﴾ is a circumstantial clause (jumla haliyya): that is, and the state is that he is in a condition contrary to the usual condition of having a father. ﴿He said: "Thus God creates what He wills"﴾ is from the speech of God, glorified is He.

The basic meaning of qada' is judgments, and it has been mentioned before. Here it means will (irada); that is, when He wills a matter among the affairs, ﴿then He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ without labor or effort, and this is an image (tamthil) for the perfection of His power.

His saying ﴿and He will teach him the Book﴾: it was said that it is conjoined to "yubashshiruka" (He gives you glad tidings); that is, God gives you glad tidings and God teaches him. It was said that it is conjoined to "yakhluqu" (He creates), that is: and thus God teaches him. Or it is a new independent sentence brought to comfort her heart.

Al-Kitab means writing (al-kitaba). Al-Hikmah means knowledge. It was said that it is refining of character. The accusative of "rasulan" is by implying "and He makes him a messenger," or "and He speaks to them as a messenger," or "and I have sent a messenger." It was also said: it is conjoined to his saying "wajihan," so it is a circumstantial state, because it has the meaning of speech, that is: and speaking. Al-Akhfash said: if you wish, you may make the waw in his saying "wa rasulan" an interpolated waw (waw muqhama), and make "al-rasul" a circumstantial state.

His saying ﴿that I have come to you﴾ is governed by "rasul," because it contains the meaning of speech, as has passed. It was said that its origin is "bi-anni qad ji'tukum," and the preposition was omitted. It was said that it is governed by a hidden verb, that is, "saying that I have come to you." It was said that it is conjoined to the earlier states. His saying "with a sign" (bi-ayah) is in the accusative position as a circumstantial state; that is, clothed with a sign from your Lord.

His saying "that I create" means: I shape and determine. ﴿for you out of clay, like the form of a bird﴾. This clause is a substitute for the first clause, which is ﴿that I have come to you﴾, or a substitute for "sign," or the predicate of an implied subject, that is: it is "that I." It is read with a kasra on the hamza as a resumption (isti'naf). Al-A'raj and Abu Ja'far read "kahay'at al-tayr" with shadda. The kaf in his saying "kahay'at al-tayr" is an adjective of an implied verbal noun (masdar), that is: I create for you a creation, or a thing like the form of a bird.

His saying "then I breathe into it" means: into that creation, or that thing; so the pronoun refers to the kaf in his saying "kahay'at al-tayr." It was said: the pronoun refers to the bird, that is, one individual of it. It was said: it refers to the clay. It was read "fa-yakunu tairan" and "tairan," like tajir and tajr. It was said that he created nothing but the bat, because of the wonders of its craftsmanship.

Indeed, it has a teat, teeth and an ear, it menstruates and becomes pure. It was said that they asked him to create a bat because of the wonders mentioned, and because it flies without feathers, and gives birth as the rest of animals give birth, despite being of the birds, and does not lay eggs as the rest of birds lay eggs. It cannot see in the light of day nor in the darkness of night; it only sees in two hours: one hour after sunset, and one hour after the dawn breaks. It laughs as a human laughs. It was said that their question to him was in the manner of provocation. It was said that it would fly as long as the people were looking at it, and when it disappeared from their eyes it fell dead, so that the act of God would be distinguished from the act of others.

His saying "by God's permission" contains evidence that, without permission from God, mighty and majestic, he would not have been able to do that, and that the creation of that was by the act of God, glorified is He, which He caused to happen through the hand of ʿIsa, peace be upon him. It was said: the shaping of the clay and the breathing were from ʿIsa, and the creating was from God, mighty and majestic.

His saying ﴿and I heal the blind-born﴾: al-akmah is one who is born blind. So said Abu ʿUbayda. Ibn Faris said: al-kamah is blindness with which a person is born, and it may also occur later. It is said: kamiha yakmahu kamahan, when he became blind, and kamihtu aynahu, when I made his eye blind. It was also said: al-akmah is one who sees by day and does not see by night. It was also said: he is one whose eye has been wiped.

Al-Baras is well known, and it is a whiteness that appears in the skin. ʿIsa, peace be upon him, used to heal many diseases, as the Gospel contains. God, glorified is He, specifically mentioned these two diseases because they generally are not cured by treatment. Likewise the raising of the dead: the Gospel contains stories of that.

His saying ﴿and I inform you of what you eat﴾: that is, I tell you of what you eat and of what you store. His saying "wa musaddiqan" (confirming) is conjoined to his saying "wa rasulan." It was also said: the meaning is "and I have come to you confirming."

His saying "wa li-uhilla" means: and in order that I make lawful; that is, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, and I have come to you to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you of foods in the Torah, such as fats and every animal with claws. It was said: he only made lawful for them what the rabbis had forbidden them and what the Torah had not forbidden. Abu ʿUbayda said: it is possible that "baʿd" (some) has the meaning of "kull" (all), and he recited:

"Tarrak amkinatin idha lam arduha aw yartabit baʿd al-nufus himamuha"

Al-Qurtubi said: this view is an error according to the people of reasoning among the linguists, because "baʿd" and "juz'" do not mean "kull," and because ʿIsa did not make lawful for them all that the Torah had forbidden them. He did not make lawful killing, nor theft, nor adultery, nor other forbidden things established in the Gospel while they are also established in the Torah. These are many, as whoever knows both books recognizes. However, "baʿd" may take the place of "kull" with a clear context, like the poet's saying:

"Aba Mundhir afnayta fa-istabqi baʿdana * hanaynaka baʿd al-sharr ahwan min baʿd"

That is: "some of evil is easier than some of it," meaning: some of the evil is easier than all of it.

قَوْلُهُ: فَلَمّا أحَسَّ أيْ عَلِمَ ووَجَدَ: قالَهُ الزَّجّاجُ: وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ مَعْنى أحَسَّ عَرَفَ، وأصْلُ ذَلِكَ وُجُودُ الشَّيْءِ بِالحاسَّةِ، والإحْساسُ: العِلْمُ بِالشَّيْءِ. قالَ اللَّهُ تَعالى: ﴿هَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنهم مِن أحَدٍ﴾ [مريم: ٩٨]. والمُرادُ بِالإحْساسِ هُنا الإدْراكُ القَوِيُّ الجارِي مَجْرى المُشاهَدَةِ. وبِالكُفْرِ إصْرارُهم عَلَيْهِ، وقِيلَ: سَمِعَ مِنهم كَلِمَةَ الكُفْرِ. وقالَ الفَرّاءُ: أرادُوا قَتْلَهُ. وعَلى هَذا فَمَعْنى الآيَةِ: فَلَمّا أدْرَكَ مِنهم عِيسى إرادَةَ قَتْلِهِ الَّتِي هي كُفْرٌ قالَ: ﴿مَن أنْصارِي إلى اللَّهِ﴾. الأنْصارُ جَمْعُ نَصِيرٍ.

وقَوْلُهُ: إلى اللَّهِ، مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِمَحْذُوفٍ وقَعَ حالًا؛ أيْ: مُتَوَجِّهًا إلى اللَّهِ ومُلْتَجِئًا إلَيْهِ أوْ ذاهِبًا إلَيْهِ. وقِيلَ: إلى بِمَعْنى مَعَ كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى ﴿ولا تَأْكُلُوا أمْوالَهم إلى أمْوالِكُمْ﴾ [النساء: ٢]. وقِيلَ: المَعْنى: مَن أنْصارِي في السَّبِيلِ إلى اللَّهِ، وقِيلَ: المَعْنى: مَن يَضُمُّ نُصْرَتَهُ إلى نُصْرَةِ اللَّهِ. والحَوارِيُّونَ جَمْعُ حَوارِيٍّ، وحَوارِيُّ الرَّجُلِ: صَفْوَتُهُ وخُلاصَتُهُ، وهو مَأْخُوذٌ مِنَ الحَوَرِ وهو البَياضُ عِنْدَ أهْلِ اللُّغَةِ، حَوَّرْتُ الثِّيابَ بَيَّضْتُها. والحَوارِيُّ مِنَ الطَّعامِ: ما حُوِّرَ؛ أيْ: بُيِّضَ. والحَوارِيُّ أيْضًا النّاصِرُ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ (ﷺ): «لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ حَوارِيٌّ وحَوارِيِّي الزُّبَيْرُ» وهو في البُخارِيِّ وغَيْرِهِ.

وقَدِ اخْتُلِفَ في سَبَبِ (p-221) تَسْمِيَتِهِمْ بِذَلِكَ، فَقِيلَ: لِبَياضِ ثِيابِهِمْ، وقِيلَ: لِخُلُوصِ نِيّاتِهِمْ، وقِيلَ: لِأنَّهم خاصَّةُ الأنْبِياءِ، وكانُوا اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ رَجُلًا. ومَعْنى أنْصارِ اللَّهِ: أنْصارُ دِينِهِ ورُسُلِهِ. وقَوْلُهُ: آمَنّا بِاللَّهِ اسْتِئْنافٌ جارٍ مَجْرى العِلَّةِ لِما قَبْلَهُ، فَإنَّ الإيمانَ يَبْعَثُ عَلى النُّصْرَةِ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿واشْهَدْ بِأنّا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ أيِ: اشْهَدْ لَنا يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ بِأنّا مُخْلِصُونَ لِإيمانِنا مُنْقادُونَ لِما تُرِيدُ مِنّا. ومَعْنى بِما أنْزَلْتَ ما أنْزَلَهُ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ في كُتُبِهِ.

والرَّسُولُ عِيسى، وحَذْفُ المُتَعَلِّقِ مُشْعِرٌ بِالتَّعْمِيمِ؛ أيِ: اتَّبَعْناهُ في كُلِّ ما يَأْتِي بِهِ فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ لَكَ بِالوَحْدانِيَّةِ ولِرَسُولِكَ بِالرِّسالَةِ. أوِ اكْتُبْنا مَعَ الأنْبِياءِ الَّذِينَ يَشْهَدُونَ لِأُمَمِهِمْ، وقِيلَ: مَعَ أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ (ﷺ).

قَوْلُهُ: ومَكَرُوا أيِ الَّذِينَ أحَسَّ عِيسى مِنهُمُ الكُفْرَ، وهم كُفّارُ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ. ومَكْرُ اللَّهِ اسْتِدْراجُهُ لِلْعِبادِ مِن حَيْثُ لا يَعْلَمُونَ.

قالَهُ الفَرّاءُ وغَيْرُهُ. وقالَ الزَّجّاجُ: مَكْرُ اللَّهِ مُجازاتُهم عَلى مَكْرِهِمْ، فَسُمِّيَ الجَزاءُ بِاسْمِ الِابْتِداءِ كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿اللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ﴾ [البقرة: ١٥]، ﴿وهُوَ خادِعُهُمْ﴾ [النساء: ١٤٢]. وأصْلُ المَكْرِ في اللُّغَةِ: الِاغْتِيالُ والخَدْعُ، حَكاهُ ابْنُ فارِسٍ، وعَلى هَذا فَلا يُسْنَدُ إلى اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ إلّا عَلى طَرِيقِ المُشاكَلَةِ. وقِيلَ: مَكْرُ اللَّهِ هُنا إلْقاءُ شِبْهِ عِيسى عَلى غَيْرِهِ، ورَفْعُ عِيسى إلَيْهِ. ﴿واللَّهُ خَيْرُ الماكِرِينَ﴾ أيْ: أقْواهم مَكْرًا وأنْفَذُهم كَيْدًا وأقْواهم عَلى إيصالِ الضَّرَرِ بِمَن يُرِيدُ إيصالَهُ بِهِ مِن حَيْثُ لا يَحْتَسِبُ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿إذْ قالَ اللَّهُ ياعِيسى﴾ العامِلُ في إذْ: مَكَرُوا، أوْ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿خَيْرُ الماكِرِينَ﴾، أوْ فِعْلٌ مُضْمَرٌ تَقْدِيرُهُ وقَعَ ذَلِكَ. وقالَ الفَرّاءُ: إنَّ في الكَلامِ تَقْدِيمًا وتَأْخِيرًا تَقْدِيرُهُ إنِّي رافِعُكَ ومُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ومُتَوَفِّيكَ بَعْدَ إنْزالِكَ مِنَ السَّماءِ.

وقالَ أبُو زَيْدٍ: مُتَوَفِّيكَ قابِضُكَ. وقالَ في الكَشّافِ: مُسْتَوْفِي أجَلَكَ، ومَعْناهُ: إنِّي عاصِمُكَ مِن أنْ يَقْتُلَكَ الكُفّارُ، ومُؤَخِّرٌ أجَلَكَ إلى أجَلٍ كَتَبْتُهُ لَكَ، ومُمِيتُكَ حَتْفَ أنْفِكَ لا قَتْلًا بِأيْدِيهِمْ.

وإنَّما احْتاجَ المُفَسِّرُونَ إلى تَأْوِيلِ الوَفاةِ بِما ذُكِرَ؛ لِأنَّ الصَّحِيحَ أنَّ اللَّهَ رَفَعَهُ إلى السَّماءِ مِن غَيْرِ وفاةٍ، كَما رَجَّحَهُ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ المُفَسِّرِينَ، واخْتارَهُ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ الطَّبَرِيُّ، ووَجْهُ ذَلِكَ أنَّهُ قَدْ صَحَّ في الأخْبارِ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) نُزُولُهُ وقَتْلُهُ الدَّجّالَ. وقِيلَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحانَهُ تَوَفّاهُ ثَلاثَ ساعاتٍ مِن نَهارٍ ثُمَّ رَفَعَهُ إلى السَّماءِ، وفِيهِ ضَعْفٌ. وقِيلَ: المُرادُ بِالوَفاةِ هُنا النَّوْمُ، ومِثْلُهُ ﴿وهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفّاكم بِاللَّيْلِ﴾ [الأنعام: ٦٠] أيْ يُنِيمُكم، وبِهِ قالَ كَثِيرُونَ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ أيْ مِن حَيْثُ جَوازُهم بِرَفْعِهِ إلى السَّماءِ وبُعْدِهِ عَنْهم.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وجاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾ أيِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا ما جِئْتَ بِهِ، وهم خُلَّصُ أصْحابِهِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا في الغُلُوِّ فِيهِ إلى ما بَلَغَ مِن جَعْلِهِ إلَهًا، ومِنهُمُ المُسْلِمُونَ، فَإنَّهُمُ اتَّبَعُوا ما جاءَ بِهِ عِيسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ ووَصَفُوهُ بِما يَسْتَحِقُّهُ مِن دُونِ غُلُوٍّ، فَلَمْ يُفَرِّطُوا في وصْفِهِ كَما فَرَّطَتِ اليَهُودُ، ولا أفْرَطُوا كَما أفْرَطَتِ النَّصارى. وقَدْ ذَهَبَ إلى هَذا كَثِيرٌ مِن أهْلِ العِلْمِ.

وقِيلَ: المُرادُ بِالآيَةِ أنَّ النَّصارى الَّذِينَ هم أتْباعُ عِيسى لا يَزالُونَ ظاهِرِينَ عَلى اليَهُودِ غالِبِينَ لَهم قاهِرِينَ لِمَن وُجِدَ مِنهم، فَيَكُونُ المُرادُ بِالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هُمُ اليَهُودُ خاصَّةً. وقِيلَ: هُمُ الرُّومُ لا يَزالُونَ ظاهِرِينَ عَلى مَن خالَفَهم مِنَ الكافِرِينَ. وقِيلَ: هُمُ الحَوارِيُّونَ لا يَزالُونَ ظاهِرِينَ عَلى مَن كَفَرَ بِالمَسِيحِ. وعَلى كُلِّ حالٍ فَغَلَبَةُ النَّصارى لِطائِفَةٍ مِنَ الكُفّارِ أوْ لِكُلِّ طَوائِفِ الكُفّارِ لا يُنافِي كَوْنَهم مَقْهُورِينَ مَغْلُوبِينَ بِطَوائِفِ المُسْلِمِينَ، كَما تُفِيدُهُ الآياتُ الكَثِيرَةُ، بِأنَّ هَذِهِ المِلَّةَ الإسْلامِيَّةَ ظاهِرَةٌ عَلى كُلِّ المِلَلِ، قاهِرَةٌ لَها مُسْتَعْلِيَةٌ عَلَيْها. وقَدْ أفْرَدْتُ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ بِمُؤَلَّفٍ سَمَّيْتُهُ (وابِلُ الغَمامَةِ في تَفْسِيرِ ﴿وجاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾)، فَمَن رامَ اسْتِيفاءَ ما في المَقامِ فَلْيَرْجِعْ إلى ذَلِكَ.

والفَوْقِيَّةُ هُنا هي أعَمُّ مِن أنْ تَكُونَ بِالسَّيْفِ أوْ بِالحُجَّةِ. وقَدْ ثَبَتَ في الأحادِيثِ الصَّحِيحَةِ أنَّ عِيسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ يَنْزِلُ في آخِرِ الزَّمانِ فَيَكْسِرُ الصَّلِيبَ، ويَقْتُلُ الخِنْزِيرَ، ويَضَعُ الجِزْيَةَ، ويَحْكُمُ بَيْنَ العِبادِ بِالشَّرِيعَةِ المُحَمَّدِيَّةِ، ويَكُونُ المُسْلِمُونَ أنْصارَهُ وأتْباعَهُ إذْ ذاكَ، فَلا يَبْعُدُ أنْ يَكُونَ في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ إشارَةٌ إلى هَذِهِ الحالَةِ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ثُمَّ إلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ﴾ أيْ رُجُوعُكم، وتَقْدِيمُ الظَّرْفِ لِلْقَصْرِ. ﴿فَأحْكُمُ بَيْنَكم﴾ يَوْمَئِذٍ ﴿فِيما كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ مِن أُمُورِ الدِّينِ. وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَأمّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿واللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ تَفْسِيرٌ لِلْحُكْمِ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فِي الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ﴾ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِقَوْلِهِ: فَأُعَذِّبُهم. أمّا تَعْذِيبُهم في الدُّنْيا فَبِالقَتْلِ والسَّبْيِ والجِزْيَةِ والصَّغارِ، وأمّا في الآخِرَةِ فَبِعَذابِ النّارِ.

قَوْلُهُ: " فَنُوَفِّيهِمْ أُجُورَهم " أيْ: نُعْطِيهِمْ إيّاها كامِلَةً مُوَفَّرَةً، قُرِئَ بِالتَّحْتِيَّةِ وبِالنُّونِ.

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يُحِبُّ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ كِنايَةٌ عَنْ بُغْضِهِمْ، وهي جُمْلَةٌ تَذْيِيلِيَّةٌ مُقَرِّرَةٌ لِما قَبْلَها. قَوْلُهُ: " ذَلِكَ " إشارَةٌ إلى ما سَلَفَ مِن نَبَأِ عِيسى وغَيْرِهِ، وهو مُبْتَدَأٌ خَبَرُهُ ما بَعْدَهُ، و" مِنَ الآياتِ " حالٌ أوْ خَبَرٌ بَعْدَ خَبَرٍ.

والحَكِيمُ المُشْتَمِلُ عَلى الحُكْمِ أوِ المُحْكَمُ الَّذِي لا خَلَلَ فِيهِ. وقَدْ أخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَلَمّا أحَسَّ عِيسى مِنهُمُ الكُفْرَ﴾ قالَ: كَفَرُوا وأرادُوا قَتْلَهُ، فَذَلِكَ حِينَ اسْتَنْصَرَ قَوْمَهُ.

وأخْرَجَ عَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ وابْنُ جَرِيرٍ وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: إنَّما سُمُّوا الحَوارِيِّينَ لِبَياضِ ثِيابِهِمْ كانُوا صَيّادِينَ. وأخْرَجَ عَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ عَنِ الضَّحّاكِ قالَ: الحَوارِيُّونَ قَصّارُونَ مَرَّ بِهِمْ عِيسى فَآمَنُوا بِهِ.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنْ قَتادَةَ قالَ: الحَوارِيُّونَ هُمُ الَّذِينَ تَصْلُحُ لَهُمُ الخِلافَةُ. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ مَرْدَوَيْهِ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: هم أصْفِياءُ الأنْبِياءِ. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنِ الضَّحّاكِ مِثْلَهُ. وأخْرَجَ عَبْدُ الرَّزّاقِ وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنْ قَتادَةَ قالَ: الحَوارِيُّ الوَزِيرُ. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنْ سُفْيانَ بْنِ عُيَيْنَةَ قالَ: الحَوارِيُّ النّاصِرُ. وأخْرَجَ عَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ وأبُو الشَّيْخِ والطَّبَرانِيُّ وابْنُ مَرْدَوَيْهِ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾ قالَ: مَعَ مُحَمَّدٍ وأُمَّتِهِ أنَّهم شَهِدُوا لَهُ أنَّهُ قَدْ بَلَّغَ، وشَهِدُوا لِلرُّسُلِ أنَّهم (p-222) قَدْ بَلَّغُوا.

وأخْرَجَ عَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ عَنْ طَرِيقِ الكَلْبِيِّ عَنْ أبِي صالِحٍ عَنْهُ قالَ: ﴿مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾ مَعَ أصْحابِ مُحَمَّدٍ (ﷺ). وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ عَنِ السُّدِّيِّ قالَ: إنَّ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ حَصَرُوا عِيسى وتِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ رَجُلًا مِنَ الحَوارِيِّينَ في بَيْتٍ، فَقالَ عِيسى لِأصْحابِهِ: مَن يَأْخُذُ صُورَتِي فَيُقْتَلُ ولَهُ الجَنَّةُ، فَأخَذَها رَجُلٌ مِنهم وصَعِدَ عِيسى إلى السَّماءِ، فَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومَكَرُوا ومَكَرَ اللَّهُ واللَّهُ خَيْرُ الماكِرِينَ﴾.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ﴾ يَقُولُ: مُمِيتُكَ. وأخْرَجَ عَبْدُ الرَّزّاقِ وابْنُ جَرِيرٍ وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنِ الحَسَنِ قالَ: مُتَوَفِّيكَ مِنَ الأرْضِ.

وأخْرَجَ الآخَرانِ عَنْهُ قالَ: وفاةُ المَنامِ. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنْ قَتادَةَ قالَ: هَذا مِنَ المُقَدَّمِ والمُؤَخَّرِ؛ أيْ: رافِعُكَ إلَيَّ ومُتَوَفِّيكَ.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنْ مَطَرٍ الوَرّاقِ قالَ: مُتَوَفِّيكَ مِنَ الدُّنْيا ولَيْسَ بِوَفاةِ مَوْتٍ. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنْ وهْبٍ قالَ: تَوَفّى اللَّهُ عِيسى ثَلاثَ ساعاتٍ مِنَ النَّهارِ حَتّى رَفَعَهُ إلَيْهِ. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ عَساكِرَ عَنْهُ قالَ: أماتَهُ ثَلاثَةَ أيّامٍ ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُ ورَفَعَهُ.

وأخْرَجَ الحاكِمُ عَنْهُ قالَ: تَوَفّى اللَّهُ عِيسى سَبْعَ ساعاتٍ. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ سَعْدٍ وأحْمَدُ في الزُّهْدِ والحاكِمُ عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ المُسَيَّبِ قالَ: رُفِعَ عِيسى وهو ابْنُ ثَلاثٍ وثَلاثِينَ سَنَةً.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ عَساكِرَ عَنْ وهْبٍ مِثْلَهُ. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ وابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنِ الحَسَنِ في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ومُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ قالَ: طَهَّرَهُ مِنَ اليَهُودِ والنَّصارى والمَجُوسِ ومِن كُفّارِ قَوْمِهِ.

وأخْرَجَ عَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ وابْنُ جَرِيرٍ عَنْ قَتادَةَ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وجاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ قالَ: هم أهْلُ الإسْلامِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ عَلى فِطْرَتِهِ ومِلَّتِهِ وسُنَّتِهِ. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ نَحْوَهُ.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ عَنِ الحَسَنِ نَحْوَهُ أيْضًا. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ وابْنُ عَساكِرَ عَنِ النُّعْمانِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ قالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) يَقُولُ: «لا تَزالُ طائِفَةٌ مِن أُمَّتِي عَلى الحَقِّ ظاهِرِينَ لا يُبالُونَ بِمَن خالَفَهم حَتّى يَأْتِيَ أمْرُ اللَّهِ». قالَ النُّعْمانُ: مَن قالَ: إنِّي أقُولُ عَلى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ما لَمْ يَقُلْ، فَإنَّ تَصْدِيقَ ذَلِكَ في كِتابِ اللَّهِ، قالَ اللَّهُ: ﴿وجاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ﴾ الآيَةَ.

وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ عَساكِرَ عَنْ مُعاوِيَةَ مَرْفُوعًا نَحْوَهُ، ثُمَّ قَرَأ مُعاوِيَةُ الآيَةَ. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ عَنِ ابْنِ زَيْدٍ قالَ: النَّصارى فَوْقَ اليَهُودِ إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ، ولَيْسَ بَلَدٌ فِيهِ أحَدٌ مِنَ النَّصارى إلّا وهم فَوْقَ اليَهُودِ في شَرْقٍ ولا غَرْبٍ، هم في البُلْدانِ كُلِّها مُسْتَذَلُّونَ.

قَوْلُهُ: فَلَمّا أحَسَّ أيْ عَلِمَ ووَجَدَ: قالَهُ الزَّجّاجُ: وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ مَعْنى أحَسَّ عَرَفَ، وأصْلُ ذَلِكَ وُجُودُ الشَّيْءِ بِالحاسَّةِ، والإحْساسُ: العِلْمُ بِالشَّيْءِ. قالَ اللَّهُ تَعالى: ﴿هَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنهم مِن أحَدٍ﴾ [مريم: ٩٨]. والمُرادُ بِالإحْساسِ هُنا الإدْراكُ القَوِيُّ الجارِي مَجْرى المُشاهَدَةِ. وبِالكُفْرِ إصْرارُهم عَلَيْهِ، وقِيلَ: سَمِعَ مِنهم كَلِمَةَ الكُفْرِ. وقالَ الفَرّاءُ: أرادُوا قَتْلَهُ. وعَلى هَذا فَمَعْنى الآيَةِ: فَلَمّا أدْرَكَ مِنهم عِيسى إرادَةَ قَتْلِهِ الَّتِي هي كُفْرٌ قالَ: ﴿مَن أنْصارِي إلى اللَّهِ﴾. الأنْصارُ جَمْعُ نَصِيرٍ.

وقَوْلُهُ: إلى اللَّهِ، مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِمَحْذُوفٍ وقَعَ حالًا؛ أيْ: مُتَوَجِّهًا إلى اللَّهِ ومُلْتَجِئًا إلَيْهِ أوْ ذاهِبًا إلَيْهِ. وقِيلَ: إلى بِمَعْنى مَعَ كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى ﴿ولا تَأْكُلُوا أمْوالَهم إلى أمْوالِكُمْ﴾ [النساء: ٢]. وقِيلَ: المَعْنى: مَن أنْصارِي في السَّبِيلِ إلى اللَّهِ، وقِيلَ: المَعْنى: مَن يَضُمُّ نُصْرَتَهُ إلى نُصْرَةِ اللَّهِ. والحَوارِيُّونَ جَمْعُ حَوارِيٍّ، وحَوارِيُّ الرَّجُلِ: صَفْوَتُهُ وخُلاصَتُهُ، وهو مَأْخُوذٌ مِنَ الحَوَرِ وهو البَياضُ عِنْدَ أهْلِ اللُّغَةِ، حَوَّرْتُ الثِّيابَ بَيَّضْتُها. والحَوارِيُّ مِنَ الطَّعامِ: ما حُوِّرَ؛ أيْ: بُيِّضَ. والحَوارِيُّ أيْضًا النّاصِرُ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ (ﷺ): «لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ حَوارِيٌّ وحَوارِيِّي الزُّبَيْرُ» وهو في البُخارِيِّ وغَيْرِهِ.

وقَدِ اخْتُلِفَ في سَبَبِ (p-221) تَسْمِيَتِهِمْ بِذَلِكَ، فَقِيلَ: لِبَياضِ ثِيابِهِمْ، وقِيلَ: لِخُلُوصِ نِيّاتِهِمْ، وقِيلَ: لِأنَّهم خاصَّةُ الأنْبِياءِ، وكانُوا اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ رَجُلًا. ومَعْنى أنْصارِ اللَّهِ: أنْصارُ دِينِهِ ورُسُلِهِ. وقَوْلُهُ: آمَنّا بِاللَّهِ اسْتِئْنافٌ جارٍ مَجْرى العِلَّةِ لِما قَبْلَهُ، فَإنَّ الإيمانَ يَبْعَثُ عَلى النُّصْرَةِ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿واشْهَدْ بِأنّا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ أيِ: اشْهَدْ لَنا يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ بِأنّا مُخْلِصُونَ لِإيمانِنا مُنْقادُونَ لِما تُرِيدُ مِنّا. ومَعْنى بِما أنْزَلْتَ ما أنْزَلَهُ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ في كُتُبِهِ.

والرَّسُولُ عِيسى، وحَذْفُ المُتَعَلِّقِ مُشْعِرٌ بِالتَّعْمِيمِ؛ أيِ: اتَّبَعْناهُ في كُلِّ ما يَأْتِي بِهِ فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ لَكَ بِالوَحْدانِيَّةِ ولِرَسُولِكَ بِالرِّسالَةِ. أوِ اكْتُبْنا مَعَ الأنْبِياءِ الَّذِينَ يَشْهَدُونَ لِأُمَمِهِمْ، وقِيلَ: مَعَ أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ (ﷺ).

قَوْلُهُ: ومَكَرُوا أيِ الَّذِينَ أحَسَّ عِيسى مِنهُمُ الكُفْرَ، وهم كُفّارُ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ. ومَكْرُ اللَّهِ اسْتِدْراجُهُ لِلْعِبادِ مِن حَيْثُ لا يَعْلَمُونَ.

قالَهُ الفَرّاءُ وغَيْرُهُ. وقالَ الزَّجّاجُ: مَكْرُ اللَّهِ مُجازاتُهم عَلى مَكْرِهِمْ، فَسُمِّيَ الجَزاءُ بِاسْمِ الِابْتِداءِ كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿اللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ﴾ [البقرة: ١٥]، ﴿وهُوَ خادِعُهُمْ﴾ [النساء: ١٤٢]. وأصْلُ المَكْرِ في اللُّغَةِ: الِاغْتِيالُ والخَدْعُ، حَكاهُ ابْنُ فارِسٍ، وعَلى هَذا فَلا يُسْنَدُ إلى اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ إلّا عَلى طَرِيقِ المُشاكَلَةِ. وقِيلَ: مَكْرُ اللَّهِ هُنا إلْقاءُ شِبْهِ عِيسى عَلى غَيْرِهِ، ورَفْعُ عِيسى إلَيْهِ. ﴿واللَّهُ خَيْرُ الماكِرِينَ﴾ أيْ: أقْواهم مَكْرًا وأنْفَذُهم كَيْدًا وأقْواهم عَلى إيصالِ الضَّرَرِ بِمَن يُرِيدُ إيصالَهُ بِهِ مِن حَيْثُ لا يَحْتَسِبُ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿إذْ قالَ اللَّهُ ياعِيسى﴾ العامِلُ في إذْ: مَكَرُوا، أوْ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿خَيْرُ الماكِرِينَ﴾، أوْ فِعْلٌ مُضْمَرٌ تَقْدِيرُهُ وقَعَ ذَلِكَ. وقالَ الفَرّاءُ: إنَّ في الكَلامِ تَقْدِيمًا وتَأْخِيرًا تَقْدِيرُهُ إنِّي رافِعُكَ ومُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ومُتَوَفِّيكَ بَعْدَ إنْزالِكَ مِنَ السَّماءِ.

وقالَ أبُو زَيْدٍ: مُتَوَفِّيكَ قابِضُكَ. وقالَ في الكَشّافِ: مُسْتَوْفِي أجَلَكَ، ومَعْناهُ: إنِّي عاصِمُكَ مِن أنْ يَقْتُلَكَ الكُفّارُ، ومُؤَخِّرٌ أجَلَكَ إلى أجَلٍ كَتَبْتُهُ لَكَ، ومُمِيتُكَ حَتْفَ أنْفِكَ لا قَتْلًا بِأيْدِيهِمْ.

وإنَّما احْتاجَ المُفَسِّرُونَ إلى تَأْوِيلِ الوَفاةِ بِما ذُكِرَ؛ لِأنَّ الصَّحِيحَ أنَّ اللَّهَ رَفَعَهُ إلى السَّماءِ مِن غَيْرِ وفاةٍ، كَما رَجَّحَهُ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ المُفَسِّرِينَ، واخْتارَهُ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ الطَّبَرِيُّ، ووَجْهُ ذَلِكَ أنَّهُ قَدْ صَحَّ في الأخْبارِ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) نُزُولُهُ وقَتْلُهُ الدَّجّالَ. وقِيلَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحانَهُ تَوَفّاهُ ثَلاثَ ساعاتٍ مِن نَهارٍ ثُمَّ رَفَعَهُ إلى السَّماءِ، وفِيهِ ضَعْفٌ. وقِيلَ: المُرادُ بِالوَفاةِ هُنا النَّوْمُ، ومِثْلُهُ ﴿وهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفّاكم بِاللَّيْلِ﴾ [الأنعام: ٦٠] أيْ يُنِيمُكم، وبِهِ قالَ كَثِيرُونَ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ أيْ مِن حَيْثُ جَوازُهم بِرَفْعِهِ إلى السَّماءِ وبُعْدِهِ عَنْهم.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وجاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾ أيِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا ما جِئْتَ بِهِ، وهم خُلَّصُ أصْحابِهِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا في الغُلُوِّ فِيهِ إلى ما بَلَغَ مِن جَعْلِهِ إلَهًا، ومِنهُمُ المُسْلِمُونَ، فَإنَّهُمُ اتَّبَعُوا ما جاءَ بِهِ عِيسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ ووَصَفُوهُ بِما يَسْتَحِقُّهُ مِن دُونِ غُلُوٍّ، فَلَمْ يُفَرِّطُوا في وصْفِهِ كَما فَرَّطَتِ اليَهُودُ، ولا أفْرَطُوا كَما أفْرَطَتِ النَّصارى. وقَدْ ذَهَبَ إلى هَذا كَثِيرٌ مِن أهْلِ العِلْمِ.

وقِيلَ: المُرادُ بِالآيَةِ أنَّ النَّصارى الَّذِينَ هم أتْباعُ عِيسى لا يَزالُونَ ظاهِرِينَ عَلى اليَهُودِ غالِبِينَ لَهم قاهِرِينَ لِمَن وُجِدَ مِنهم، فَيَكُونُ المُرادُ بِالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هُمُ اليَهُودُ خاصَّةً. وقِيلَ: هُمُ الرُّومُ لا يَزالُونَ ظاهِرِينَ عَلى مَن خالَفَهم مِنَ الكافِرِينَ. وقِيلَ: هُمُ الحَوارِيُّونَ لا يَزالُونَ ظاهِرِينَ عَلى مَن كَفَرَ بِالمَسِيحِ. وعَلى كُلِّ حالٍ فَغَلَبَةُ النَّصارى لِطائِفَةٍ مِنَ الكُفّارِ أوْ لِكُلِّ طَوائِفِ الكُفّارِ لا يُنافِي كَوْنَهم مَقْهُورِينَ مَغْلُوبِينَ بِطَوائِفِ المُسْلِمِينَ، كَما تُفِيدُهُ الآياتُ الكَثِيرَةُ، بِأنَّ هَذِهِ المِلَّةَ الإسْلامِيَّةَ ظاهِرَةٌ عَلى كُلِّ المِلَلِ، قاهِرَةٌ لَها مُسْتَعْلِيَةٌ عَلَيْها. وقَدْ أفْرَدْتُ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ بِمُؤَلَّفٍ سَمَّيْتُهُ (وابِلُ الغَمامَةِ في تَفْسِيرِ ﴿وجاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾)، فَمَن رامَ اسْتِيفاءَ ما في المَقامِ فَلْيَرْجِعْ إلى ذَلِكَ.

والفَوْقِيَّةُ هُنا هي أعَمُّ مِن أنْ تَكُونَ بِالسَّيْفِ أوْ بِالحُجَّةِ. وقَدْ ثَبَتَ في الأحادِيثِ الصَّحِيحَةِ أنَّ عِيسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ يَنْزِلُ في آخِرِ الزَّمانِ فَيَكْسِرُ الصَّلِيبَ، ويَقْتُلُ الخِنْزِيرَ، ويَضَعُ الجِزْيَةَ، ويَحْكُمُ بَيْنَ العِبادِ بِالشَّرِيعَةِ المُحَمَّدِيَّةِ، ويَكُونُ المُسْلِمُونَ أنْصارَهُ وأتْباعَهُ إذْ ذاكَ، فَلا يَبْعُدُ أنْ يَكُونَ في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ إشارَةٌ إلى هَذِهِ الحالَةِ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ثُمَّ إلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ﴾ أيْ رُجُوعُكم، وتَقْدِيمُ الظَّرْفِ لِلْقَصْرِ. ﴿فَأحْكُمُ بَيْنَكم﴾ يَوْمَئِذٍ ﴿فِيما كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ مِن أُمُورِ الدِّينِ. وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَأمّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿واللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ تَفْسِيرٌ لِلْحُكْمِ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فِي الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ﴾ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِقَوْلِهِ: فَأُعَذِّبُهم. أمّا تَعْذِيبُهم في الدُّنْيا فَبِالقَتْلِ والسَّبْيِ والجِزْيَةِ والصَّغارِ، وأمّا في الآخِرَةِ فَبِعَذابِ النّارِ.

قَوْلُهُ: " فَنُوَفِّيهِمْ أُجُورَهم " أيْ: نُعْطِيهِمْ إيّاها كامِلَةً مُوَفَّرَةً، قُرِئَ بِالتَّحْتِيَّةِ وبِالنُّونِ.
